articles.title: Countries demand Israel lift Gaza aid restrictions as Palestinians suffer
articles.summary: Qatar, Turkiye and six other countries urge ‘unimpeded’ humanitarian access to Gaza as Israel cracks down on aid groups.
articles.body:
Several countries in the Middle East and Asia have called on Israel to allow “immediate, full, and unhindered” deliveries of humanitarian aid to the Gaza Strip as winter storms lash the bombarded Palestinian enclave.

In a statement on Friday, the foreign ministers of Qatar, Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Turkiye, Pakistan and Indonesia warned that “deteriorating” conditions in Gaza had left nearly 1.9 million displaced Palestinians particularly vulnerable.

“Flooded camps, damaged tents, the collapse of damaged buildings, and exposure to cold temperatures coupled with malnutrition, have significantly heightened risks to civilian lives,” the statement reads.

They called on the international community “to pressure Israel, as the occupying power, to immediately lift constraints on the entry and distribution of essential supplies including tents, shelter materials, medical assistance, clean water, fuel, and sanitation support”.

Israel has maintained stringent restrictions on the entry of humanitarian aid into Gaza despite its obligations under international law to ensure that the basic needs of Palestinians in the enclave are met.

A United States-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Hamas, which came into effect in October, also stipulated that the Israeli authorities must allow hundreds of aid trucks into Gaza daily.

But Israel has failed to abide by that requirement, continuing to block deliveries despite increasingly difficult winter conditions in the coastal territory and a lack of adequate shelter, blankets and other supplies.

Hundreds of thousands of Palestinian families have sought refuge in makeshift shelters and overcrowded tent encampments across Gaza because their homes were destroyed in Israel’s genocidal war.

Several people were killed in recent weeks as damaged buildings collapsed under the weight of heavy rainfall and flooding. Palestinian children have also died from hypothermia as low temperatures continue to grip the enclave.

Separately on Friday, Israeli forces killed one Palestinian and injured several others west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, Nasser Hospital said.

Four Palestinians, including a woman and two children, were seriously wounded after an Israeli drone fired a grenade at a tent housing displaced people in Beit Lahiya in the north of the Strip, a source at al-Shifa Hospital told Al Jazeera.

In Friday’s statement, the foreign ministers commended the United Nations and other humanitarian groups for continuing to support Palestinians “under extremely difficult and complex circumstances” in Gaza.

They also demanded that Israel allow UN agencies and international nonprofit organisations to operate in Gaza and the occupied West Bank “in a sustained, predictable, and unrestricted manner” given the role they play in providing humanitarian support.

“Any attempt to impede their ability to operate is unacceptable,” they said.

The condemnation comes as Israel this week moved to implement a ban on 37 international NGOs working in Gaza and the West Bank for failing to meet new registration requirements.

Experts have denounced the Israeli government’s new rules – which require the targeted groups to provide detailed information on their staff members, funding and operations – as arbitrary and a violation of humanitarian principles.

The NGOs have also raised concerns that giving Israel personal information about their Palestinian employees puts those workers at risk of being targeted by the Israeli military.

According to Gaza’s Government Media Office, Israel has killed about 500 aid workers and volunteers in the enclave since its war began in October 2023.

Doctors Without Borders, one of the groups targeted by the NGO ban, noted in a statement on Friday that 15 of its colleagues have been killed by Israeli forces.

“In any context – especially one where medical and humanitarian workers have been intimidated, arbitrarily detained, attacked, and killed in large numbers – demanding staff lists as a condition for access to territory is an outrageous overreach,” the organisation said.

articles.title: See how gas prices have changed in your county since the Iran war began
articles.summary: How much gas prices have increased during the Iran war depends entirely on where you live, an NBC News analysis of average gas price data from AAA shows.
articles.body: Gas prices are up across the country, but nowhere are they up as much as in Johnson County, Wyo., where an average gallon of gas would run you $4.37 a gallon Friday, 70% more than the price at the start of the Iran war. How much gas prices have increased depends on where you live, an NBC News analysis of average gas price data from AAA shows. Johnson County’s price was up $1.81 a gallon, while Fisher County, Texas, population 3,600, prices had only increased 51 cents as of Friday. It also depends on the state. In Indiana, average gas prices are up $0.78 per gallon, among the lowest state-level increases in the nation (Indiana has repeatedly suspended its state gas tax). But in Montana, the average price is up $1.52 per gallon, the largest state-level increase in the U.S. This map, showing the latest county-level gas prices and the change in prices since the start of the war, will be updated daily. Polling consistently indicates that prices and the economy rank among voters’ top issues ahead of the midterm elections. An April poll showed gas prices were a problem for nearly two-thirds of Americans. As of early May, counties have seen increases of an average of $1.47 per gallon. However, about 100 counties, mostly in Indiana and Ohio, have seen price increases of $2 per gallon or more. Conversely, a little more than a dozen counties — mostly in Georgia and Nebraska — have seen price increases of less than $1 per gallon. See the trends of gas prices nationally and on the state level with the NBC News gas price tracker, and calculate how much the gas price increase has cost you with the the NBC News gas cost calculator.

articles.title: Iran jails psychologist over Trump plea as regime demands he make Americans ‘look stupid’: family
articles.summary: Seyed Ahmad Seyedabdollahi was sentenced to seven months in prison by the Islamic Republic after posting a video appealing to Trump to support protesters.
articles.body: FIRST ON FOX: An Iranian psychologist who publicly appealed to President Donald Trump to stand by Iranians protesting the Islamic Republic has been sentenced to seven months in prison, while his relatives say authorities tried to pressure him into recording a video insulting Trump and Americans. Seyed Ahmad Seyedabdollahi, a 32-year-old psychologist and counselor from Borujen who had been living in Tehran, posted an English-language video on Jan. 4 directly addressing Trump. In the video, reviewed by Fox News Digital, he urged the president to act quickly on his pledge to support Iranian protesters, saying young Iranians had trusted his words and that those who helped the Iranian people would be remembered. ""...To prove your good intentions to the Iranian people, either do something without saying anything or act very quickly on your words, because many young people trust what you say. And, as you probably know, many things are useless to people who are dead.I assure you that the Iranian nation remembers good deeds well, and they will try to repay their friends in the future." TRUMP ADMIN BYPASSES TEHRAN'S ISOLATION CAMPAIGN TO REACH IRANIANS DIRECTLY Ten days later, on Jan. 14, Seyedabdollahi was arrested at his father's home in Borujen, according to Iran International, Iran Wire, Harana human rights activist news agency, and the Hana Human Rights Organization. Hana reported that plainclothes agents confiscated phones and electronic equipment and that Seyedabdollahi was subsequently held in solitary confinement and at an Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps intelligence detention facility in Isfahan. A relative of Seyedabdollahi told Fox News Digital that the video triggered sustained pressure from Iranian security authorities. "Since that day, he has faced serious pressure from Iranian security authorities. He was arrested twice and subjected to repeated interrogations," the relative said. "During his detention, he spent extended periods in solitary confinement. He was eventually convicted and sentenced to seven months in prison, and in July 2026 he was transferred to prison to begin serving his sentence." Branch One of the Borujen Revolutionary Court convicted Seyedabdollahi of "engaging in media activities against national security," sentenced him to seven months in prison and barred him from government and public services for five years, Iran International reported Aug. 6. He was detained again July 7 to begin serving the sentence and remains in Borujen Prison. IRAN INMATES SEW LIPS SHUT IN MASS HUNGER STRIKE AT NOTORIOUS US-SANCTIONED JAIL: REPORT Hana Human Rights Organization said he was denied contact with his family for 17 days following his first arrest and that his family initially did not know where he was being held. Iran International reported that he was denied access to a lawyer of his choosing during his detention and at times was prevented from communicating with his family. Iranian authorities have also opened a second case against Seyedabdollahi on a charge translated as "propaganda against the establishment" or "propaganda against the system of the Islamic Republic." The case, opened in June, remains at the preliminary investigative stage, according to Hana. Court documents obtained by Fox News Digital appear to detail the authorities' investigation of Seyedabdollahi and contain references to alleged foreign contacts and financial transactions involving the United States and Israel. His relative said interrogators accused him of being connected to the CIA and Mossad and of receiving money in exchange for making the video. "They told him you are a member of the CIA and Mossad and you took money from them for this job," the relative said. AIR FORCE INTEL VET ALLEGEDLY SPIRALED INTO IRAN’S TERROR UNDERWORLD: TIMELINE OF DECEIT, HUNT FOR SPY SUSPECT The relative also alleged that Iranian authorities pressured Seyedabdollahi to record another video repudiating his original message and attacking Trump and Americans. "He did not give in to numerous pressures to publish a clip that contradicted the first video," the relative said. "He was asked to sexually insult Trump and make the American people look stupid and ignorant so that we could broadcast your clip on the national media." The relative further alleged that Seyedabdollahi endured solitary confinement and mistreatment during interrogations, and said he continues to face pressure in prison after refusing authorities' demands. Those allegations also could not be independently verified. "His situation in Borujen Prison is not good because he has been out of solitary confinement for a few days, but sometimes they take him to solitary confinement under various pretexts," the relative said, adding that monitored telephone calls make it difficult for him to speak openly about his treatment. FREED AMERICAN REVEALS BRUTAL IRAN PRISON ORDEAL, WARNS HOSTAGES FACE GREATER DANGER The relative said the five-year prohibition on public and government employment has compounded the punishment by threatening Seyedabdollahi's ability to work after his release. "You understand the economic conditions of Iran. Now imagine that in this situation someone has been deprived of their social rights, i.e. job and income, and he is imprisoned," the relative said. The relative described Seyedabdollahi as a psychologist and popular speaker with a following among young Iranians, and said he remained focused on those who suffered more severely during the government's crackdown. In the brief period when he was free, the relative recalled him saying, "Don't feel weak. Our problems are insignificant compared to the thousands of people who have lost their lives." Seyedabdollahi was one of several Iranians who directly appealed to Trump during January's nationwide protests. Iran International reported that he posted his video Jan. 4, two days after Trump warned Iranian authorities against firing on peaceful demonstrators. Trump again warned Tehran on Jan. 9 and on Jan. 13 urged Iranians to continue protesting, writing that "help is on its way." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Iran International reported that the crackdown resulted in mass arrests and cited the U.S.-based Human Rights Activists News Agency as saying more than 50,000 people were arrested during a period of just over six weeks. The outlet also reported that U.N. human rights chief Volker Türk said at least 56 people had been executed on national-security-related charges since March 19, including 27 in cases linked to the January protests. The Iranian mission to the U.N. declined to comment.

articles.title: The most iconic breakfast restaurant in every state
articles.summary: From diners to brunch spots, here are some of the most iconic restaurants to grab breakfast in every state.
articles.body:
Breakfast restaurants across the country are known for their loyal followings.

Café du Monde in New Orleans and Lou Mitchell's in Chicago are among the most iconic spots.

Here are the most famous or iconic breakfast restaurants in every state.

Breakfast is often cited as the most important meal of the day, so why waste it on a bowl of cereal?

Across the country, hole-in-the-wall diners , cozy cafés, and decades-old institutions have become known for signature breakfast dishes, famous customers, or simply for serving generations of loyal regulars.

While there might be some debate about which spot is truly the most iconic, we identified famous breakfast restaurants in every state based on their longevity, reputation, famous dishes, and local history.

From beignets at New Orleans' Café du Monde to classic Southern breakfasts at The Waysider in Tuscaloosa, these restaurants offer more than a good plate of eggs and pancakes — they offer a slice of local pride.

Here are some of the most iconic breakfast restaurants in every state.

ALABAMA: The Waysider Restaurant in Tuscaloosa

The Waysider is a Tuscaloosa institution. In fact, it's the city's oldest operating restaurant . Legendary Alabama football coach Bear Bryant was a regular, and the restaurant is still filled with memorabilia for all devoted Roll Tide fans to enjoy.

It's known for classic Southern breakfasts, including biscuits, grits, country ham, and gravy.

Snow City Cafe has been a popular downtown Anchorage breakfast spot since its opening in 1998.

During a 2015 visit to the state, President Barack Obama stopped by the cafe and ordered $18.25 worth of cinnamon rolls and muffins to go, the Anchorage Daily News reported.

The menu includes Alaskan takes on breakfast classics, including eggs Benedict with salmon cakes.

ARIZONA: Matt's Big Breakfast in Phoenix

Matt's Big Breakfast opened in downtown Phoenix in 2004 in a small, 800-square-foot space. It quickly became known for its long lines. They've since expanded into a larger location due to demand.

The restaurant focuses on simple breakfasts made with high-quality ingredients, including cage-free eggs, freshly squeezed orange juice, and real maple syrup.

The restaurant later appeared on an episode of Guy Fieri's "Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives," cementing its status as a local legend.

ARKANSAS: The Pancake Shop in Hot Springs

The Pancake Shop has served breakfast in downtown Hot Springs since 1940, making it one of the city's longtime dining institutions.

The restaurant is known for its made-from-scratch pancakes, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and homemade sausage, and its original 1940 menu still hangs inside for patrons to see.

CALIFORNIA: Du-par's Restaurant & Bakery in Los Angeles

Du-par's has been a local institution since James Dunn and Edward Parsons opened it at the Original Farmers Market in Los Angeles in 1938.

The restaurant is best known for its buttermilk hotcakes, made with the same recipe the kitchen used in 1938. Along with its famous pancakes, the longtime diner is known for other classic American comfort foods, diner favorites, and housemade pies and pastries.

COLORADO: Snooze, an A.M. Eatery in Denver

Opened by brothers Adam and Jon Schlegel in Denver's Ballpark neighborhood in 2006, Snooze has become one of Denver's best-known brunch spots.

It later expanded into a national chain and now operates about 70 locations across 10 states.

It's particularly known for creative pancake flavors, eggs Benedict, and its pancake flight, which lets diners choose several pancake flavors.

Laurel Diner has been serving Southbury since 1949 and retains the feel of a traditional roadside diner. The small cash-only restaurant still has its counter stools and serves classic diner breakfasts, including its best-known dish, its house-made corned beef hash and home fries.

Kozy Korner traces its history to 1922, when John Vouras opened the original restaurant in Wilmington.

Although its original building was demolished in 1984, the family-run restaurant continued in a new location with another crowd-pleasing menu.

The restaurant has been repeatedly recognized by Delaware Today for serving the best breakfast in the state, according to its website .

Blue Heaven, which is located in a venue with a history tied to Ernest Hemingway, opened in Key West's Bahama Village in 1992.

The restaurant is known for its outdoor courtyard, roaming chickens, and live music, as well as its popular breakfast favorites , including eggs Benedict, shrimp and grits, and pancakes.

Home Grown, which opened in Atlanta in 2010, has become one of the city's best-known breakfast spots, serving traditional Southern comfort food in a casual, retro-country diner setting.

Featured in the Michelin Guide, the restaurant is especially famous for its Comfy Chicken Biscuit, which combines fried chicken, a large Southern biscuit, and sausage gravy.

Eggs 'n Things, which has been serving breakfast in Honolulu since 1974, has largely become known for its large breakfast plates, particularly pancakes topped with local fruit and generous amounts of whipped cream.

The restaurant's popularity in the community and among tourists has led to additional locations in Guam, Hawaii, and Japan.

IDAHO: Goldy's Breakfast Bistro in Boise

Goldy's Breakfast Bistro has been a downtown Boise breakfast destination since 1999.

The small restaurant is known for its eggs Benedict and large breakfast plates, including diner favorites such as chicken-fried steak.

Lou Mitchell's has been serving Chicago since 1923, predating the establishment of nearby Route 66 by three years.

Its location near the highway's historic starting point made the restaurant a longtime stop for travelers beginning the drive west, and it's also listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

The restaurant is also known for handing out complimentary doughnut holes to customers waiting for a table — a tradition that dates back decades.

The first Cafe Patachou opened in Indianapolis in 1989, and the café has since built its reputation on made-to-order breakfasts and relationships with local farmers and producers.

Bon Appétit later named it one of the country's best breakfast spots, according to the restaurant's website .

Waveland Cafe has been serving Des Moines since 1984 and is best known for its hash browns, which the restaurant calls the "best hashbrowns in the galaxy."

Its customers over the years have included politicians, journalists, and celebrities, including Iowa local Jason Momoa, who called the establishment his favorite breakfast spot.

The restaurant even named its signature breakfast, the "Da Momoa," after the actor. It includes a full order of hash browns, a full order of biscuits and gravy, two sunny-side-up eggs, and a side of bacon.

Doo-Dah Diner opened in Wichita in 2012 and built a following with its oversize takes on classic breakfast plates and complimentary sticky monkey bread.

Other menu favorites include banana-bread French toast and the Brutus, which combines chicken-fried steak, hash browns, sausage gravy, onions, and eggs.

KENTUCKY: Wagner's Pharmacy in Louisville

Open since 1922, Wagner's Pharmacy has been located across from Churchill Downs and has spent much of that time feeding horse trainers, jockeys, owners, and racing fans who gather there from near and far.

Its walls are covered in horse-racing memorabilia, and the restaurant has appeared in movies including "Secretariat," making it a local institution, particularly during Derby season.

Café du Monde has been serving customers in New Orleans' French Market since 1862. Its menu is famously limited, with its best-known order consisting of three fried beignets covered in powdered sugar and a cup of chicory coffee or café au lait.

The combination has become one of the foods most closely associated with New Orleans , making the café not just a breakfast spot but also a tourist destination.

Palace Diner may be small, but it is entirely worth the cramped quarters. The restaurant, housed in a former train dining car, has been in operation since 1927.

Visitors flock to the unique restaurant for a classic diner breakfast, fried chicken sandwich, and other diner specialties.

MARYLAND: Miss Shirley's Cafe in Baltimore

Miss Shirley's Cafe has been putting a Maryland spin on Southern breakfast since it opened in Baltimore in 2005.

Named after founder Eddie Dopkin's friend Shirley McDowell, the restaurant is known for dishes like shrimp and grits, chicken and waffles, and several takes on eggs Benedict.

In a state famous for seafood, the menu also finds plenty of ways to bring local flavors into brunch.

MASSACHUSETTS: Miss Florence Diner in Florence

Miss Florence Diner doesn't have to try overly hard or stock up on kitschy decor to look like an old-fashioned diner.

Operating from a preserved Worcester Lunch Car Company dining car, the vintage diner still has many of its original features and was even added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1999.

More than 80 years after its founding, it's still serving pancakes, eggs, bacon, and other classic New England diner breakfasts.

This small Lansing restaurant is covered in colorful signs, stickers, and artwork inside and out, making it hard to miss when driving through town.

In addition to its quirky decor, this restaurant is equally well known for its over-the-top breakfasts, from creative pancakes and French toast to massive omelets. It's also known for long waits, limited seating, and a daily menu written on whiteboards that changes frequently.

MINNESOTA: Al's Breakfast in Minneapolis

Al's Breakfast in the city's Dinkytown neighborhood has been a Minneapolis institution since 1950, and customers regularly line up behind the restaurant's limited number of stools waiting for their turn to eat.

The tiny restaurant has also received one of the industry's biggest honors — a James Beard America's Classics award — and has also been featured on "Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives."

MISSISSIPPI: Big Bad Breakfast in Oxford

Big Bad Breakfast has expanded across the South, but it got its start in Oxford in 2008. The restaurant comes from James Beard Award-winning chef John Currence, who built the menu around Southern breakfast staples like biscuits, grits, eggs, and house-cured meats.

Its success in Oxford eventually turned Big Bad Breakfast into a regional chain with locations across several states.

MISSOURI: Billy Gail's Restaurant in Branson

Billy Gail's is the kind of breakfast place where ordering pancakes can become a photo opportunity. The Branson-area restaurant is famous for its enormous omelets and pancakes, which stretch well beyond the edges of the plate, along with oversize portions of biscuits and gravy, French toast, and other diner favorites.

The large portions and cozy diner setting have made it a popular breakfast stop for visitors and locals alike.

The Western Cafe has been part of downtown Bozeman since it opened in the 1940s and is now run by three generations of the same Montana family.

Its menu is about as Montana as breakfast gets, with dishes like chicken-fried steak and eggs, biscuits and gravy, and its famous "Bobcat" French toast, a nod to the nearby Montana State University.

You might want to bring someone along if you're looking to split a cinnamon roll at Tina's Cafe.

This small Lincoln restaurant is known for scratch-made cinnamon rolls that are roughly the size of a dinner plate and dripping with icing, along with hand-shredded hash browns and other classic breakfasts.

NEVADA: The Peppermill Restaurant and Fireside Lounge in Las Vegas

The Peppermill has been serving the Las Vegas Strip since 1972, and its neon-lit, over-the-top interior still pays homage to that era. The restaurant is known for large breakfast portions and its adjoining Fireside Lounge, complete with a sunken fire pit.

The restaurant has also appeared in iconic movies and TV shows, including "Casino," and in 2024, the James Beard Foundation named the Peppermill an America's Classics award winner.

NEW HAMPSHIRE: Polly's Pancake Parlor in Sugar Hill

Polly's Pancake Parlor has been serving pancakes in New Hampshire's White Mountains since 1938, when Polly and Wilfred Dexter began making them to promote their homemade maple products. Back then, you could order all-you-can-eat pancakes, waffles, and French toast for 50 cents.

The restaurant won a James Beard America's Classics award in 2006.

Tops Diner in East Newark, New Jersey, opened in 1942 and has been serving its iconic breakfast plates, burgers, meatloaf, and famous disco fries ever since.

In 2017, Time Out named Tops the best diner in the country, and in 2015, Thrillist called it the "most iconic" restaurant in New Jersey.

Frontier has been a favorite among University of New Mexico students and Albuquerque locals since it opened in 1971.

It's best known for Southwestern breakfast staples like burritos, homemade tortillas, and its famous Frontier Sweet Roll, a large cinnamon roll.

NEW YORK: Clinton St. Baking Company in New York City

Clinton St. Baking Company has been open on the Lower East Side of Manhattan since 2001 and has become known for its fluffy pancakes with specialty toppings like maple butter or wild Maine blueberries.

Prepare to wait a while to grab breakfast here — wait times can stretch up to two hours at peak weekend brunch times.

NORTH CAROLINA: Big Ed's City Market Restaurant in Raleigh

Big Ed's was opened in 1958 by Wake County native "Big Ed" Watkins, who used recipes from his family's farm to inspire the first menu.

The City Market location opened in 1989 and has become one of the most popular breakfast destinations in Raleigh, specializing in old-fashioned North Carolina country breakfasts with plenty of biscuits, eggs, country ham, and grits.

NORTH DAKOTA: The Shack on Broadway in Fargo

The Shack on Broadway isn't anything fancy, but its all-day breakfast has kept locals coming back again and again.

Famous for its buttermilk pancakes, omelets, hash browns, and other classic diner breakfast staples, this breakfast spot's straightforward menu has made it a longtime favorite in Fargo.

Sugar n' Spice has served the Cincinnati community since 1941, and very little has changed at the diner since then.

Known for its thin pancakes and fluffy, oversize omelets, this longtime favorite breakfast spot also sends each guest home with something less edible, but just as memorable: tiny rubber ducks.

Cafe Kacao, which opened in 2006, stands out among Oklahoma City institutions for its focus on Guatemalan and Latin American flavors.

Featured on Yelp's list of the 100 best restaurants in the country and named best breakfast in Oklahoma by the Travel Channel, one bite of this family-owned restaurant's breakfast will show you why it's so acclaimed.

Otis Cafe was originally housed in an iconic historic building before a 2019 fire forced it to relocate to a new location in the Taft district.

This family-run restaurant is known for serving scratch-made breakfast all day and for a few German breakfast classics, including German-style potatoes and marionberry pie.

PENNSYLVANIA: Shady Maple Smorgasbord in East Earl

Shady Maple is one of the most famous breakfast buffets in the country, but even that reputation doesn't quite capture its scale.

Opened in 1985, Shady Maple has grown into a 161,000-square-foot restaurant that can seat nearly 1,200 people at one time.

Its breakfast offerings include an enormous spread of eggs, pancakes, meats, baked goods, and Pennsylvania Dutch specialties — all served in what has been described as the largest buffet in the country.

While Rhode Island may be better known for its seafood, this classic Ocean State diner also reflects the small state's culinary history.

Housed inside a 1940 Sterling Streamliner, Modern Diner was the first diner in the country to be accepted onto the National Register of Historic Places — it was listed in 1978. It is a Pawtucket landmark, famous for its classic breakfast plates and distinctive decor.

SOUTH CAROLINA: Millers All Day in Charleston

Millers All Day may not be the most historic restaurant on this list, but it's just as iconic.

Opened in 2018 and helmed by chef Nathan Thurston and farmer and miller Greg Johnsman, the menu features a modern spin on classic Southern breakfast favorites like biscuit sandwiches and shrimp and grits.

SOUTH DAKOTA: Phillips Avenue Diner in Sioux Falls

Phillips Avenue Diner is known throughout the state for its retro feel and massive breakfast plates, including pancakes, omelets, and other classic American breakfast items.

The restaurant operated as the Market Diner inside a silver Airstream trailer until 1996, when it moved to downtown Sioux Falls and became known as the Phillips Avenue Diner in a new brick-and-mortar location.

TENNESSEE: The Loveless Cafe in Nashville

The Loveless Cafe opened in 1951, when Lon and Annie Loveless began serving homemade fried chicken and biscuits to travelers from their home along Highway 100. Their food was so popular that the Lovelesses turned their house into a full-blown restaurant and added a 14-room motel to expand their business.

More than 70 years later, Annie's famous biscuits are still a signature item on the menu, and the Nashville landmark welcomes more than half a million visitors a year, according to the restaurant's website .

Opened in 2001, The Breakfast Klub has become one of Houston's most iconic institutions, thanks to its famous "Katfish" and grits and wings and waffles.

The Black-owned restaurant has garnered national recognition from outlets including "Good Morning America," USA Today, Esquire, and Forbes.

Ruth's Diner allows guests to dine in a former trolley car that operated in the early 1900s, but has since been moved and restored. The restaurant focuses on brunch foods, serving cinnamon roll French toast, huevos rancheros, and deep-fried mac and cheese.

When " Diners, Drive-Ins, and Dives " host Guy Fieri visited the restaurant, he said he couldn't get enough of the fluffy biscuits.

VERMONT: Maple Sugar & Vermont Spice in Mendon

Perhaps nothing is more signature Vermont than pancakes with maple syrup. Maple Sugar & Vermont Spice is located right where the action is, on the grounds of a historic Mendon maple farm, where visitors can watch sap being boiled into syrup.

In addition to pancakes, guests can try the famous syrup with other breakfast staples, or purchase maple candy and other products to take home.

VIRGINIA: Pocahontas Pancake in Virginia Beach

Pocahontas Pancake and Waffle House has been serving up breakfast in the Virginia Beach oceanfront area since 1974, but rose to national fame in 2002 when the Food Network's "Best Of" series named it the best pancake house in Virginia Beach.

Its most popular menu item is, unsurprisingly, its pancakes drenched in butter and maple syrup, but it also serves other breakfast staples like Belgian waffles, French toast, eggs, and omelets.

Built in 1937, Maltby Cafe has served breakfasts for decades from the basement of a former schoolhouse gym.

The restaurant is known locally for its massive portions and oversize cinnamon rolls, which have become one of the café's signature dishes.

If there's one item this Beckley diner is famous for, it's omelets.

The restaurant serves breakfast around the clock, seven days a week, making it a favorite for locals and travelers looking for eggs, pancakes, biscuits and gravy, and, of course, omelets at any hour.

Franks Diner has been serving the city of Kenosha since 1926 in an original Jerry O'Mahony lunch car, where it still stands today.

Wisconsin's oldest continuously operating diner , this local favorite is best known for its Garbage Plate: a hefty breakfast of eggs, hash browns, meat, cheese, and vegetables that has become the diner's signature dish.

WYOMING: Nora's Fish Creek Inn in Wilson

Nora's Fish Creek Inn has been a Jackson Hole breakfast staple since Nora and Marvin Tygum opened it in 1982.

Housed inside a rustic 1930s-era log cabin, the restaurant is famous for its large portions of breakfast favorites like huevos rancheros and pancakes, as well as fresh pan-fried Idaho trout.

articles.summary: Durante a agenda, ele também prometeu apoiar trabalhadores na informalidade e trabalhadores por app.
articles.body:
Ciro Gomes (PSDB) visita o Centro de Fortaleza em ato de campanha neste sábado (29). — Foto: Kid Júnior/SVM

O candidato ao governo do Ceará, Ciro Gomes (PSDB), afirmou neste sábado (29), durante evento de campanha no Centro de Fortaleza , que irá recorrer da decisão do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Ceará (TRE-CE) que liberou a publicação de vídeo em que o senador Camilo Santana associa Ciro ao candidato à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) . Durante a agenda, ele também prometeu apoiar trabalhadores na informalidade e trabalhadores por app.

"Eu vou recorrer por uma única razão. A razão é que isso é mentira. É simples assim. Porque eu podia dizer em qualquer lugar e digo aqui que o Elmano é eleitor do Ronaldo Caiado. Aí alguém ia dizer: 'Não, seu Ciro tá mentindo'. Mas como eu sou sério e respeito as pessoas, eu não vou dizer que o Elmano é eleitor do Ronaldo Caiado porque ele entregou ao partido do Ronaldo Caiado a vice-governadoria dele próprio [em referência a Gabriella Aguiar, candidata a vice de Elmano, que é do PSD, partido de Caiado]", afirmou Ciro.

No vídeo em questão, publicado no Instagram, Facebook, TikTok e X (antigo Twitter), Camilo afirmou que "Ciro é o candidato de Flávio Bolsonaro no Ceará". No último dia 24, o juiz auxiliar do TRE determinou que o conteúdo fosse removido no prazo de 24 horas. No entanto, na sexta-feira (28), o tribunal liberou o conteúdo.

Ao comentar a decisão de liberação, Ciro destacou que ainda não definiu seu apoio presidencial, mas agradece os votos de eleitores de qualquer candidato a presidente. "O que eu quero é o seguinte, cada cearense vote com a liberdade, com a esperança", concluiu.

Apoio a ambulantes e trabalhadores por app

Durante a caminhada no Centro de Fortaleza, Ciro visitou algumas lojas, cumprimentou pedestres e conversou com comerciantes. Ele citou números de trabalho informal no Ceará e a baixa média salarial no estado. Ele afirmou que, se eleito, pretende aplicar medidas para apoiar trabalhadores informais e trabalhadores por app.

"Hoje quem tá salvando o estado do Ceará é o setor de serviços, mas o setor de serviços ele tende a não ter as remunerações compatíveis com o nosso desejo", disse. "Mais da metade dos cearense estão na informalidade, sem proteção nenhuma, obrigados, como a gente sabe, a garotada do iFood, a garotada do do 99, do Uber Moto, eles estão aí trabalhando 12, 14 horas. Se quebrar a corrente da da motocicleta aquele dia ou aqueles dois dias ele não não fatura", citou o peessedebista.

Ciro disse que iria reforçar o setor de serviços por meio de capacitação profissional e voltou a citar a promessa de fazer alterações no ensino médio da rede pública estadual, inserindo capacitações em áreas de inteligência artificial e outras tecnologias.

"Nós estamos preparando todo um projeto para reforçar essa estrutura de serviços do estado do Ceará, porém puxando essa qualidade de serviço. Onde é que eu vou priorizar? Entregar no ensino médio uma capacitação para o manejo de inteligência artificial, para o manejo de aplicativos e criação de aplicativos e para o manejo de redes", disse o candidato.

articles.title: Viçosa bate recorde com lata gigante de 3 toneladas de doce de leite | G1
articles.standfirst: Ação pelos 100 anos da Universidade Federal de Viçosa distribuiu iguaria gratuitamente a uma multidão no campus da instituição. Produção mira recorde mundial.
articles.summary: Ação pelos 100 anos da Universidade Federal de Viçosa distribuiu iguaria gratuitamente a uma multidão no campus da instituição. Produção mira recorde mundial.
articles.body:
Viçosa , na Zona da Mata mineira, entrou para a história do doce de leite neste sábado (29). Para celebrar os 100 anos da Universidade Federal de Viçosa ( UFV ), foram produzidas 3,4 toneladas da iguaria, colocada em uma lata gigante e depois distribuída gratuitamente ao público.

A lata é a maior já produzida no Brasil e busca também o recorde mundial, que ainda precisa ser homologado pelo Guinness World Records. Entenda mais abaixo.

O recipiente tem 2 metros de largura por 2 metros de comprimento e foi instalado no gramado das Quatro Pilastras, no campus da universidade.

Doce de leite Viçosa foi distribuído no Campus da UFV — Foto: Larissa Zimmermann/TV Integração

Após os procedimentos de medição e certificação, o doce começou a ser distribuído gratuitamente ao público. Foram disponibilizados mais de 10 mil potes individuais de 300 g cada. Uma longa fila se formou dentro do campus da universidade para receber a iguaria.

O doce de leite é produzido pelo Laticínio Escola – Produtos Viçosa há mais de 50 anos, em uma parceria entre a universidade e a Fundação Arthur Bernardes (Funarbe).

Além da lata de doce de leite gigante, tamanho da fila para receber a iguaria também chamou atenção — Foto: Larissa Zimmermann/TV Integração

A distribuição do doce busca superar o atual recorde mundial, registrado em Celaya, no México, onde foram produzidos 2.886 kg de doce de leite em 2023, segundo o Guinness World Records.

Fiscais do RankBrasil acompanharam presencialmente os procedimentos de medição e certificação. A organização também vai enviar documentos e evidências para avaliação do Guinness World Records, responsável por homologar o eventual novo recorde.

Para produzir as 3,4 toneladas de doce de leite, foram utilizados cerca de 7,5 mil litros de leite, adquiridos de produtores rurais da região.

Comemoração pelo centenário da UFV teve distribuição de 3,4 toneladas do Doce de Leite Viçosa — Foto: Larissa Zimmermann/TV Integração

O Doce de Leite Viçosa se tornou um dos principais símbolos culturais da cidade mineira. O produto foi eleito 10 vezes o 'Melhor Doce de Leite do Brasil', passou a integrar o patrimônio cultural imaterial de Minas Gerais e chegou ao mercado internacional .

A história começou há mais de 50 anos, em um laboratório criado para apoiar as aulas práticas da UFV. Com o tempo, o espaço se transformou no Laticínio Escola, que passou a exercer um papel importante nas atividades acadêmicas da universidade.

O laticínio funciona como laboratório para ensino, pesquisa, extensão e inovação e contribui para a formação dos estudantes.

Além da versão tradicional, o Doce de Leite Viçosa é produzido nos sabores coco, café e cacau. A marca também conta com uma linha food service, voltada principalmente para o uso em recheios.

Doce já foi eleito o melhor do Brasil 10 vezes

O produto chegou ao mercado em 1988, e a primeira premiação veio em 2001. Desde então, o Doce de Leite Viçosa foi eleito 10 vezes o 'Melhor Doce de Leite do Brasil' no Concurso Nacional de Produtos Lácteos , considerado um dos principais do setor no país.

Em 2022, o processo de fabricação do Doce de Leite Tradicional Viçosa foi reconhecido como Patrimônio Cultural Imaterial de Minas Gerais. Em setembro de 2024, começou a ser exportado para os Estados Unidos .

articles.title: Mulher tem parada cardíaca e morre após acidente em Ribeirão Preto, SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima estava na garupa de uma moto. Batida aconteceu na noite desta sexta-feira (28) na Avenida Maurílio Biagi.
articles.summary: O acidente em Ribeirão Preto ocorreu na Avenida Maurílio Biagi e acabou com a morte de uma mulher de 28 anos após batida envolvendo moto e carro na noite de sexta-feira (28).
articles.body:
Uma mulher de 28 anos teve uma parada cardíaca e morreu depois da moto que ela estava bater na traseira de um carro na noite da última sexta-feira (28), em Ribeirão Preto (SP).

De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, a mulher estava na garupa da moto, caiu após a batida e morreu na hora.

O acidente aconteceu na Avenida Maurílio Biagi, Zona Sul da cidade. Até a última publicação desta reportagem ninguém tinha sido identificado.

O motociclista, de 23 anos, que conduzia a moto ficou ferido e foi encaminhado para a Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) Oeste. A pessoa que dirigia o carro não teve ferimentos, segundo o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (SAMU).

Mulher de 28 anos teve uma parada cardíaca e morreu depois de acidente em Ribeirão Preto (SP) — Foto: Reprodução/Portal SP Online

Em nota à EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo, a Secretaria de Segurança Pública informou que a perícia foi acionada e o caso foi registrado no 4º Distrito Policial de Ribeirão Preto como colisão e homicídio culposo na direção de veículo automotor .

A RP Mobi não precisou fazer interdições no local.

No fim da tarde desta sexta-feira (28), um outro acidente parecido aconteceu no bairro Cristo Redentor, Zona Norte de Ribeirão Preto. Um homem de 25 anos morreu e outras duas pessoas ficaram feridas depois que uma moto bateu na lateral de um carro.

Segundo o boletim de ocorrência, o carro atravessava um cruzamento na na Avenida Maximilliam Maggioni quando foi atingido na lateral pela motocicleta.

Com o impacto, o passageiro da moto foi arremessado. O Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foi acionado, mas a vítima não resistiu aos ferimentos.

A perícia foi acionada no local e o caso também foi registrado como colisão e homicídio culposo na direção de veículo automotor . Até a última atualização desta reportagem, a identidade de nenhuma das vítimas havia sido divulgada.

articles.title: Chuva no RS deixa dois mortos e atinge mais de 1,6 mil residências | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao todo, 21 cidades reportaram danos. Em Três Palmeiras, granizo danificou cerca de 60% da área do município e prefeitura de Quaraí decretou situação de emergência.
articles.summary: Ao todo, 21 cidades reportaram danos. Em Três Palmeiras, granizo danificou cerca de 60% da área do município e prefeitura de Quaraí decretou situação de emergência
articles.body:
A Defesa Civil do Rio Grande do Sul confirmou, na manhã deste sábado (29), mais uma morte causada pela chuva . O órgão contabiliza dois óbitos e dois feridos nos temporais registrados entre a sexta-feira (28) e a madrugada deste sábado .

Ao todo, 21 cidades gaúchas reportaram danos e mais de 1,6 mil residências foram atingidas . Há pelo menos 28 pessoas desalojadas, segundo o último boletim divulgado pela Defesa Civil estadual.

Em Arroio Grande , no Sul do estado, um homem morreu após um carro ser arrastado pela água e afundar em um arroio na noite de sexta-feira. O condutor conseguiu sair do veículo. Ele foi socorrido e levado a um hospital. O corpo do passageiro de 72 anos foi encontrado pela manhã , de acordo com a Defesa Civil.

Na sexta-feira, um menino de 8 anos morreu após uma árvore cair sobre uma casa na Zona Norte de Porto Alegre . O corpo de Wylliam Gustavo Barboza é velado neste sábado. A mãe dele ficou ferida.

A cidade mais atingida foi Três Palmeiras , no Norte do estado. O granizo provocou estragos em cerca de 60% da área do município , que tem aproximadamente 4 mil habitantes. Mil residências foram danificadas . Pessoas ficaram desabrigadas e estão sendo encaminhadas ao abrigo municipal.

Granizo atingiu mil residências em Três Palmeiras — Foto: Defesa Civil de Três Palmeiras

Em Quaraí , na Fronteira Oeste, a queda de granizo atingiu 349 casas . Devido aos estragos, a prefeitura decretou situação de emergência. Para auxiliar os moradores afetados, a Defesa Civil do município realizou a distribuição de lonas e trabalha no conserto de telhados. Sete pessoas estão desalojadas.

A Serra Gaúcha também registrou estragos causados por granizo . Moradores e turistas receberam um alerta vermelho da Defesa Civil para tempestade diretamente na tela dos celulares na noite de sexta-feira. Por volta das 22h30, pessoas que estavam em Gramado e Canela receberam o aviso da ferramenta Cell Broadcast.

Em Canela, de acordo com a Defesa Civil municipal, 197 casas foram atingidas . Lonas foram distribuídas aos moradores cujas residências tiveram telhas danificadas pelo granizo. Em Gramado, não há registro de danos.

Granizo em Gramado e Canela — Foto: Cedidas/Vitor Camargo e Defesa Civil de Canela

Em Pinheiro Machado, houve alagamentos na sede da prefeitura, em um teatro, em uma escola e em cerca de 20 residências. Também foram registrados danos em Cambará do Sul (6 residências) em Candiota (7), em Jaboticaba (32), em Liberato Salzano (30). em Pareci Novo (2), em Pelotas, em Rosário do Sul, em Santa Cruz do Sul e em Trindade do Sul.

articles.title: Em agenda no RS, Zema fala em plano de 'construção de barragens'  | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do Novo à Presidência esteve no local onde a Ponte da FelizCidade foi levada pela correnteza. Ele também cumpre agendas em Canoas e Esteio neste fim de semana.
articles.summary: Candidato do Novo à Presidência esteve no local onde a Ponte da FelizCidade foi levada pela correnteza. Ele também cumpre agendas em Canoas e Esteio neste fim de semana
articles.body:
Em agenda no Rio Grande do Sul, o candidato à Presidência da República Romeu Zema ( Novo ) esteve na manhã deste sábado (29) na cidade de Feliz , a cerca de 80 km de Porto Alegre .

"Vim aqui me solidarizar com a comunidade, com a cidade de Feliz, que teve no passado essa infelicidade de ter a ponte destruída", disse em entrevista à RBS TV.

Zema esteve na Ponte da FelizCidade, local marcado por sucessivas perdas causadas pelas enchentes . Em maio de 2024, a cheia histórica derrubou a ponte sobre o Rio Caí. Cinco meses depois, moradores arrecadaram recursos e construíram a passagem provisória.

No entanto, em janeiro de 2025, a correnteza levou embora a Ponte da FelizCidade. Após nova mobilização da comunidade, a estrutura foi reconstruída e entregue à população em março de 2026. Porém, em julho, ela voltou a ser destruída pela chuva .

O candidato afirmou que seu plano de governo prevê medidas para evitar novos desastres no estado.

"Construção de barragens para nós evitarmos esse tipo de tragédia que acometeu o Rio Grande do Sul e também um monitoramento muito mais efetivo de diversos cursos d 'água para que as comunidades sejam previamente avisadas", destaca.

Zema defende que o país precisa de obras de infraestrutura para enfrentar eventos climáticos extremos . "Um governo que vai ter recursos para investir nesses equipamentos, na modernização, ter uma previsão climática melhor e, consequentemente, evitar tragédias como a do Rio Grande do Sul em 2024", diz.

Romeu Zema (Novo) esteve na manhã deste sábado (29) na cidade de Feliz — Foto: Reprodução/RBS TV

Zema cumpre agenda no estado desde a tarde de sexta-feira (28), quando deu entrevista à Rádio Guaíba, de Porto Alegre, e participou de um encontro com pastores e de uma reunião com integrantes do Novo à noite.

Ainda neste sábado, o candidato estará em Canoas , para um evento do partido. Zema visita a Expointer, em Esteio , no domingo (30) pela manhã e, depois segue para Curitiba, no Paraná.

articles.title: Residencial Salgueiro: confira a lista de inscritos na seleção | G1
articles.standfirst: Relação com 2.138 candidatos está disponível no site do município. Próxima etapa inclui análise de elegibilidade e validação com o CadÚnico até 15 de setembro.
articles.summary: A lista do Residencial Salgueiro conta com 2.138 candidatos que passarão por análise do CadÚnico até 15 de setembro para a seleção das 112 unidades.
articles.body:
Agendamento para cadastro do Minha Casa, Minha Vida termina nesta sexta-feira em Salgueiro — Foto: Divulgação/Prefeitura de Salgueiro

A Prefeitura de Salgueiro divulgou a lista de inscritos para o processo de seleção do Residencial Salgueiro – Etapa I. A relação dos candidatos está disponível para consulta no site do município . Ao todo, 2.138 pessoas se cadastraram para disputar a entrega de 112 apartamentos.

Entre os dias 8 e 15 de setembro, o governo fará a análise de elegibilidade, a validação das inscrições por meio do CadÚnico e a hierarquização dos inscritos. A lista com os nomes das pessoas consideradas elegíveis será publicada no dia 17 de setembro. Os candidatos que desejarem apresentar recursos terão o período de 18 a 21 de setembro para contestar o resultado.

Após essa fase, ocorrerá o processo final de hierarquização. As famílias selecionadas serão convocadas para a verificação documental, agendada para o período de 8 de outubro a 11 de novembro.

O Residencial Salgueiro está em construção às margens da BR-116, na saída para o estado do Ceará. O empreendimento é uma ação do Governo de Pernambuco, por meio do Programa Morar Bem, e tem apoio operacional da prefeitura.

O projeto também conta com subsídio do programa federal Minha Casa, Minha Vida (MCMV), por meio do Fundo de Arrendamento Residencial (FAR). A parceria permite a redução das parcelas dos imóveis para um valor simbólico.

articles.title: Vídeo: boi cai em piscina e é resgatado com pá-carregadeira em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Militares encontraram o animal dentro da piscina, sem conseguir sair.
articles.summary: Militares encontraram o animal dentro da piscina, sem conseguir sair.
articles.body:
Um boi foi resgatado pelo Corpo de Bombeiros após cair em uma piscina de uma casa no bairro Jurumirim, na zona rural de Poconé , a 104 km de Cuiabá, nessa sexta-feira (28). Ao chegarem ao local, os militares encontraram o animal dentro da piscina, sem conseguir sair.

Para realizar o resgate, os bombeiros amarraram o boi e utilizaram uma pá-carregadeira da própria propriedade para retirá-lo da piscina.

Um vídeo registrado pelos bombeiros mostra o animal sendo retirado de dentro da piscina, enquanto está preso ao equipamento de segurança (vídeo acima) .

Boi caiu em piscina de casa em Poconé e precisou ser resgatado por bombeiros — Foto: Reprodução

Após o resgate, as amarras foram removidas e o animal foi entregue ao proprietário. Segundo os bombeiros, o boi não apresentava ferimentos.

Ainda conforme a corporação, não há informações sobre as circunstâncias que fizeram o animal cair na piscina.

articles.title: Boituva e Iperó mudam lei e colocam animais como seres sencientes  | G1
articles.standfirst: Senciência é a capacidade de experimentar sensações e sentimentos, como dor, medo, prazer e bem-estar. O projeto, que reconhece essa condição nos animais, foi incluído na Lei Orgânica dos dois municípios.
articles.summary: A inclusão da senciência animal na Lei Orgânica de Boituva e Iperó estabelece diretrizes para políticas públicas e proteção jurídica contra maus-tratos na região.
articles.body:
Boituva reconhece animais como seres sencientes na Lei Orgânica; Iperó também adotou medida em 2026 — Foto: Uipa Itapetininga/Divulgação

Boituva e Iperó (SP) passaram a reconhecer oficialmente os animais como seres sencientes, ou seja, capazes de sentir dor, emoções e bem-estar.

Em Boituva, a mudança foi incluída na Lei Orgânica do município por meio da Emenda à Lei Orgânica nº 2, de 4 de agosto de 2026, que acrescentou o artigo 228-B à legislação municipal.

Médica veterinária de Sorocaba (SP) orienta sobre como prevenir intoxicações por ingestão de cupins em cães e gatos — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

A lei estabelece que os animais possuem natureza biológica e emocional e devem receber proteção jurídica especial. O texto também determina que o Poder Público e a população têm o dever de protegê-los, garantindo a integridade física, o bem-estar e a prevenção de práticas de crueldade e maus-tratos.

O projeto foi elaborado e apresentado aos vereadores de Iperó e Boituva pelo advogado Valter Pietrobom Junior, morador de Boituva.

Cão Orelha morava na Praia Brava — Foto: Reprodução/Redes sociais

Ao g1, ele explicou que a proposta foi motivada pela morte do cão Orelha, ocorrida em janeiro deste ano, em uma praia de Florianópolis (SC).

"Me motivou a estudar alternativas jurídicas para endurecer as punições contra maus-tratos. Percebi que o caminho mais efetivo seria fortalecer a proteção local. Por isso, redigi uma proposta de alteração na Lei Orgânica, que é a 'Constituição' da cidade, e a entreguei aos vereadores de Iperó e Boituva para que os animais fossem reconhecidos por lei como seres sencientes, garantindo respeito à sua dor, emoções e bem-estar", explicou.

A alteração ainda prevê que o município poderá desenvolver ações, programas e políticas públicas voltadas à proteção e ao bem-estar animal, respeitando a legislação vigente e a disponibilidade orçamentária.

Conforme o advogado, a senciência é a capacidade de experimentar sensações e sentimentos, como dor, medo, prazer e bem-estar.

Na prática, o reconhecimento na legislação municipal reforça a ideia de que os animais não devem ser tratados apenas como objetos, mas como seres que merecem proteção e consideração em razão de sua capacidade de sentir.

A mudança, no entanto, não cria automaticamente novos crimes ou penas para quem maltratar animais. Essas punições continuam sendo estabelecidas por outras normas, principalmente pela legislação federal.

"A alteração na Lei Orgânica funciona como uma diretriz para a atuação do município na proteção animal", explica Valter.

Em Iperó (SP), a Emenda à Lei Orgânica nº 18, de 29 de abril de 2026, acrescentou o artigo 187-A à legislação municipal para reconhecer os animais como seres sencientes e sujeitos de direitos despersonificados. A proposta havia sido apresentada como Projeto de Emenda à Lei Orgânica nº 1/2026.

O texto de Iperó é, inclusive, mais específico ao utilizar a expressão “sujeitos de direitos despersonificados”, conceito que também aparece em legislações de outros municípios.

"É fundamental destacar que o trabalho das Procuradorias Jurídicas de ambas as Câmaras Municipais foi imprescindível. A análise técnica e o parecer impecável das procuradorias deram o embasamento necessário para a aprovação do projeto", afirma o advogado.

A mudança, no entanto, não cria automaticamente novos crimes ou penas para quem maltratar animais. — Foto: Júlia Martins/G1

Reconhecimento também existe em outras esferas

O conceito não está restrito às legislações municipais. No Distrito Federal, por exemplo, a Lei nº 7.535/2024 reconhece os animais não humanos como seres sencientes, passíveis de dor e sofrimento, e prevê tutela jurisdicional em caso de violação de seus direitos.

Em Minas Gerais, a legislação estadual também reconhece os animais como seres sencientes e sujeitos de direito despersonificados, por meio da Lei nº 23.724/2020, que acrescentou um parágrafo à Lei nº 22.231/2016, que já tratava dos maus-tratos contra animais.

Com as aprovações, Boituva e Iperó passam a integrar um grupo de municípios que adotaram expressamente o conceito de senciência animal em suas legislações.

articles.title: Fox Hollow coroner reveals why he doubts suspected serial killer acted alone in hunt for answers
articles.summary: Over 9,000 bones remain unexamined at Fox Hollow Farm as the true crime documentary explores whether suspected serial killer Herb Baumeister acted alone.
articles.body: Nearly 30 years after thousands of human bones and bone fragments were unearthed at the sprawling estate of suspected serial killer Herb Baumeister, new questions are being raised about the mystery of what really happened at Fox Hollow Farm. The coroner leading the renewed investigation claims a key figure in the case has not been fully forthcoming with investigators. "I have had an opportunity to speak with Mark Goodyear a couple of times," Hamilton County Coroner Jeff Jellison told Fox News Digital. FOX HOLLOW FARM SERIAL KILLER'S 10TH VICTIM IDENTIFIED: CORONER "The first question I would ask him is, ‘Are you ready to be honest with me?’ Because in the conversations we’ve had, he’s not been honest. I’ve asked him questions that I knew the answer to, and he didn’t pass that test. So for me to sit down with Mark Goodyear, he’s going to have to be willing to be honest in this conversation. I don’t have time to sit down with somebody that tells lies, untruths." Jellison appears in the ABC News Studios true crime documentary "Return to Fox Hollow: New Victims, Darker Secrets," which explores new theories about potential accomplices, overlooked evidence and witness accounts in the case of Baumeister, a suspected serial killer believed to have murdered numerous men in Indiana. It's a follow-up to the 2025 docuseries "The Fox Hollow Murders: Playground of a Serial Killer." Jellison said he wants to determine whether Goodyear knows something that could help investigators identify the remaining victims and determine how they died. Goodyear has never been charged with any crime related to the case and has repeatedly denied any involvement in the disappearances. "If we move forward in that conversation, certainly I want to know any information I can gather to help identify these remains," said Jellison. "Were you familiar with anybody? Things that would focus more around identification and how these people died." "Mark Goodyear knows a lot about this case," Jellison said. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X Jellison also shared that Goodyear knew many people through gay nightclubs and could help investigators identify some of the remains. Goodyear, who participated in the first docuseries, has described himself as Baumeister's only known survivor. The film detailed how investigators believed Baumeister may have filmed his victims with a secret camera hidden in an air vent in his basement. Goodyear said he was forced to watch some of the tapes in 1994. He said the video was so "bad" it made him scream. "It was like having a camera right up against something," Goodyear said. "You're not going to be able to tell what's going on, but the minute you got a flash of what was going on, it made you scream." The previous documentary examined how Goodyear's account of his relationship and encounters with Baumeister has changed over the years. At the time, Jellison told Fox News Digital it was unlikely those tapes, if they exist, would ever be recovered. Fox News Digital reached out to Goodyear for comment but did not receive a response. Goodyear initially agreed to another interview for the follow-up documentary but did not appear for the scheduled interview, according to the film. SIGN UP TO GET THE TRUE CRIME NEWSLETTER About 10,000 burned and broken human bones and bone fragments were recovered from the 18-acre estate that once belonged to Baumeister. Before investigators could arrest him in 1996, Baumeister was found dead of a self-inflicted gunshot wound in Ontario, Canada. He was 49. Investigators believe Baumeister frequented gay bars in Indianapolis, lured men to his home while his family was away, killed them there and disposed of their remains on the property. Baumeister's son discovered a human skull in the woods at Fox Hollow Farm in 1994, but, according to reports, investigators did not search the property until June 1996. Goodyear said he first encountered Baumeister at an Indianapolis gay bar in 1994, where Baumeister introduced himself as "Brian." Goodyear later told investigators that he went home with Baumeister and described what he said was a disturbing sexual encounter. Goodyear's account eventually helped advance the investigation. After encountering Baumeister again the following year, Goodyear helped investigators obtain information that led them to identify Baumeister. While Jellison has questioned Goodyear's account, he also made clear in the documentary that Goodyear was not a suspect. GET REAL-TIME UPDATES DIRECTLY ON THE TRUE CRIME HUB "There are very strong indications there is another suspect, and it wasn’t Mark Goodyear," Jellison said in the film. Jellison said there are still more than 9,000 bones and bone fragments yet to be examined. Investigators believe at least 25 people fell victim to Baumeister, according to WRTV. The scope and placement of the remains have also raised another question for Jellison: whether Baumeister could have carried out the crimes alone. "I was always convinced that there was more than one," Jellison said. "There were a lot of people that lost their lives in this incident, and just the placement of the evidence alone. How does one man pull this crime off? And how does one man get ... deceased individuals from his residence to potentially 200 yards through very dense woods? I think it would've been a very difficult task." Jellison is determined to put names to the unidentified victims. He believes some families may still be unaware that a loved one vanished or that the person's remains may have ended up at Fox Hollow Farm. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS Jellison compared the scale of the investigation to the recovery effort at the World Trade Center. "Some of these folks did not have close family connections, and they were somewhat marginalized," he explained. "So there may be families out there not even knowing that their loved one went missing, much less consider that person was a victim at Fox Hollow." GOT A TIP? "Thirty years have passed since these remains have been recovered," he reflected. "So potentially, mom and dad could be deceased, and maybe they had no brother or sister. So we’re reaching out further down the lineage to cousins. And a cousin may not even know that they had a family member that even went missing." Jellison said identifying the Fox Hollow victims presents a unique challenge. He contrasted the case with the World Trade Center investigation, where records and missing-person reports gave investigators a clearer idea of who they were looking for. At Fox Hollow, investigators started with remains but few clues about their identities. LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST "I really believe that this investigation is more complicated in some ways than the World Trade Center," he said. "With Fox Hollow, we’ve recovered these remains, but we have no idea who it is that we’re looking for." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL Jellison is urging anyone who believes a missing loved one could be connected to the case to contact his office. After the original documentary aired, his office received approximately 500 emails, phone calls, text messages and social media messages, Jellison said. SEND US A TIP "Come forward," he said. "If you don’t know what to do or you don’t know who to call, call me. I’ll get you going in the right direction."

articles.title: Andy Burnham differs from Starmer on assisted dying bill, will skip vote to avoid influencing debate
articles.summary: UK News: Unlike his predecessor Keir Starmer, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will not vote when the assisted dying bill for England and Wales returns to the Ho.
articles.body: Unlike his predecessor Keir Starmer, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will not vote when the assisted dying bill for England and Wales returns to the House of Commons next month, saying he does not want to influence the debate, according to the BBC.The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill is scheduled for its second reading in the Commons on September 11.The legislation would allow adults over 18 who are expected to die within six months to seek assistance to end their lives, subject to safeguards.In a letter to Labour MPs, Burnham said he had his "own personal views on the issue" but believed it was a matter for Parliament to decide."My role, as the prime minister, will be to lead a government that implements the will of Parliament in this area – whether that is to change the law or not," he wrote."I also do not want to unduly influence the debate as prime minister and for every colleague to know it is a genuinely free vote," Burnham added.Burnham differs from Starmer on assisted dying billBurnham's decision differs from former prime minister Keir Starmer, who voted in favour of the previous assisted dying bill at its second and third readings while maintaining the government's official neutrality on the issue, the BBC reported.The previous bill, introduced by Labour MP Kim Leadbeater, passed the Commons but failed to become law after peers in the House of Lords tabled more than 1,200 amendments, causing it to run out of parliamentary time.A near-identical bill has now been introduced by Labour MP Lauren Edwards and is expected to be debated next month.Burnham tells ministers to avoid public debateIn a separate letter to ministers, Burnham said they would be free to vote or abstain according to their conscience.However, he told them to avoid publicly trying to influence the debate and not to comment on the bill's implications for their departments."The government remains neutral on the question of assisted dying and on the passage of the bill," Burnham said.Burnham had previously indicated support for assisted dying in principle while serving as mayor of Greater Manchester.However, he later warned that implementing the policy would be challenging unless palliative and social care were improved.Supporters of the bill argue that a proposed implementation period of up to four years would provide time for improvements articles.title: Working group created to study air connectivity in Alderney
articles.summary: The group in Alderney is to oversee a review of air services between the Channel Islands and the UK.
articles.body:
A new working group has been created to oversee a review of the air services between the Channel Islands and the UK.

Alderney's Policy and Finance Committee established the Air Connectivity Oversight Working Group, comprised of States members Steve Roberts as chair, Veronica Taylor and Kevin Gentle.

The group was formed after Roberts proposed the States of Alderney commission an independent review of air services between the island, Guernsey, Jersey and the UK.

Roberts said the review would help develop an evidence-based understanding of the current challenges affecting Alderney's air connectivity.

Aurigny blamed weather conditions for most of the cancellations in the first two months of the year.

The airline said some cancellations in March had been caused by technical issues with the Twin Otter aircraft based in Guernsey and other cancellations had been caused by pilot absences .

"Recent disruption has reinforced the importance of understanding the challenges facing Alderney's air connectivity," Roberts said.

He added the first phase of the review was set to focus on gathering evidence and data on the impact of air connectivity on employment, healthcare, education, tourism, business activity and everyday life.

The working group will consider operational statistics collected by local pilots, as well as passenger survey data collected by the Alderney Chamber of Commerce, with both datasets covering the period since February 2026.

articles.title: Welsh Gender Service surgical referrals paused for clinical review
articles.summary: Data suggests "significantly higher" rates of referral for gender-affirming surgery compared with English services, according to the health board.
articles.body:
The Welsh Gender Service has paused scheduled and new referrals for gender-affirming surgeries, after the health board in charge reported "concerns" about the number of referrals being made.

Data from 2025-26 indicated "significantly higher rates of referral for gender affirming surgery... compared with English gender services", said Cardiff and Vale University Health Board.

The NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee has requested an independent clinical review after identifying "matters" through routine "assurance processes".

The health board said patients should still attend scheduled appointments and other parts of the service would continue to operate, including hormone therapy support.

The Welsh Gender Service is an NHS gender identity clinic established in 2019 which provides specialist care and support for adults in Wales. The service refers patients to England for surgery.

Cardiff and Vale University Health Board (CAVUHB), which runs the service, said it was asked to "immediately pause referrals from the Welsh Gender Service for gender affirming surgery and existing scheduled surgeries while further independent clinical review work is carried out".

"Concerns have arisen from referral data from 2025-26 indicating significantly higher rates of referral for gender affirming surgery from the Welsh Gender Service compared with English gender services," the health board said in a statement .

"In addition, concerns were raised regarding aspects of referral and assessment processes."

New referrals for gender affirming surgery have been paused

Surgical assessments and scheduled surgery have been paused

An independent clinical review will be undertaken to provide assurance about assessment, referral and governance arrangements

The health board said it understood that the announcement "may be concerning for patients, their families, staff and the wider community".

It said other parts of the service continued to operate, including hormone therapy support, psychological support and speech and language therapy.

The health board said patients who have scheduled appointments with the Welsh Gender Service should continue to attend for discussions around next steps and psychological support.

The NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee (NWJCC), which commissions national specialist services, said its "processes are designed to ensure appropriate scrutiny and oversight where further discussion or investigation is required".

articles.title: Strange Georgia crime-scene clues blow hole in theory of mom’s mysterious death, family says
articles.summary: Natalie Jones' toxicology report came back clean, yet Georgia authorities pushed an overdose theory before closing her 2020 Heard County death case.
articles.body: A negative toxicology report, missing teeth and an unusually positioned driver’s seat are fueling renewed questions into the unexplained 2020 death of Georgia mother Natalie Jones. "The Truth About Natalie," a six-part Audiochuck series, examines the 27-year-old’s life before her disappearance, the circumstances surrounding her death and a questionable overdose theory. The series draws from case files, crime-scene evidence, candid interviews with family members and a volunteer advocate, along with independent forensic analysis. Jones’ mother, Elaine Gordon, told Fox News Digital that friction with investigators began during the search. She alleged that a detective accused her of interfering as she pressed for answers. DETECTIVES' TRUE CRIME PODCAST TAKES FRESH SHOT AT KILLER WHO VANISHED AFTER CAUGHT-ON-CAMERA MURDER "What did they expect me to do, sit at home and be quiet? And I still want somebody to answer this for me: How do we even know Natalie left that lake house in the first place?" Gordon told Fox News Digital. Gordon also questioned whether investigators thoroughly interviewed everyone connected to her daughter’s final hours.
