articles.title: Dolly Parton's favorite Southern dishes, from chicken and dumplings to banana pudding
articles.summary: Country music star Dolly Parton's beloved Southern recipes included chicken and dumplings, buttermilk biscuits and gravy, banana pudding and her favorite chess pie.
articles.body: As the world mourns country music icon Dolly Parton following her death at age 80, her favorite Southern dishes offer a taste of the traditions she cherished throughout her life. "We were born cooking, as they say," Parton told Food Network of growing up as one of 12 children in Tennessee. "All of my life, I remember being in the kitchen with somebody because life just centered around the kitchen." Parton said she learned to cook from "all those wonderful relatives" she watched in the kitchen. 'GOLDEN GIRLS' KITCHEN COMES TO LIFE WITH CHEESECAKE AND '80S NOSTALGIA "If I were giving you tips, I'd probably get a notice from the health department because I like to use a lot of butter," she told Food Network. "You've got to use a little bit of the things that really make things taste good if you're going after that soul food, so to speak. You've gotta use some grease — bacon grease, mainly." The signature dishes Parton said she often prepared and liked to eat showcased her Southern roots. She published two cookbooks: "Dolly's Dixie Fixin's" in 2006 and, with her sister Rachel Parton George, "Good Lookin' Cookin'" in 2024. Parton also endorsed several food and cooking products, including cake mixes and frozen meals, throughout her career. FROM FONDUE TO CASSEROLES: CLASSIC 1960S FOODS THAT DEFINED A GENERATION "I'm a really, really good cook," Parton told Wired in 2020. "I'm not a gourmet cook. My food is not pretty, but it's good." Below are some of the Queen of Country Music's favorite foods. Chicken and dumplings A recipe for the Southern classic appeared in "Dollywood Presents: Tennessee Mountain Home Cooking," published in 1989. Decades later, Parton said in an interview with Country Living, "When I think about my mama, I think about some chicken and dumplings." 6 ICONIC AMERICAN RESTAURANTS STILL SERVING UP NOSTALGIA AND CLASSIC FLAVORS "I like a good meatloaf. It's easy to make," she told the publication. "But I also love to make chicken and dumplings. I get a couple of chickens, and I get enough for everyone because everyone loves my chicken and dumplings!" The 1989 recipe associated with Parton begins by simmering a whole chicken with onion and celery leaves in salted water, according to The Kitchn. Parton said it would take her "all day" to make chicken and dumplings the way she liked them. "I may read a while or try to relax while I check in on my cooking," she told Country Living. "It's the same thing with a meatloaf or fried chicken." But Parton wouldn't give away all the details of her famous dish. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "I don't give out the recipe," she said. "Mine is all these secret ingredients — and the main one is love." Biscuits and gravy One of Parton's favorite breakfast foods was biscuits and gravy. "Everybody makes biscuits, but how many people make buttermilk biscuits unless you really are from the South?" Parton said in a 2023 interview with Eater. "I love it all. I eat gravy and biscuits at least once a week for breakfast with sausage or whatever. With the same pan, I'll get a biscuit and put apple butter or jam or jelly on there. Whatever looks good. There’s no bad way to eat a biscuit." Banana pudding Parton described herself as more of a cook than a baker, but banana pudding was among her favorite desserts. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "Everybody loves banana pudding," she said on ABC's "Good Morning America" in 2022. "That was always one of my favorite things, a big old bowl of banana puddin'." A recipe for the Southern staple, inspired by her mother's method, is included in "Dolly's Dixie Fixin's" and calls for a 12-ounce box of vanilla wafers and five to six sliced bananas. Potatoes Parton admitted to Wired that potatoes were her weakness. "Every diet I ever fell off of has been because of a potato," Parton said. "Either french fries or mashed potatoes or baked potatoes. Potato, potato, potato! I never met a spud I didn't like." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Parton said a mayonnaise-based potato salad was her go-to dish to bring to a barbecue. She recalled that Sunday fried chicken served with potato salad was "one of the greatest things ever" from her childhood. "When that happened at our church and that big bowl of potato salad got there, you didn't have to worry," she said during an interview on the "Today" show in 2022. "Even [if] it was sunny, it wasn't gonna last that long! It wasn't gonna go bad … not if I was around!" Roast pork Another love of Parton's was roast pork, "especially the fatty part," Parton said in a 1992 interview with The New York Times. "I can't help it. The greasier the food, the better." Parton revealed to the Times in 1992 that one of her favorite meals to serve guests was roast pork with green beans, turnip greens and fried okra. Chess pie Chess pie, a traditional Southern custard-style pie typically made with eggs, sugar, butter and flour or cornmeal, was Parton's favorite pie, she told USA Today in 2019. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I don't eat much cake," she said. "I usually have pie on my birthday. My favorite pie is chess pie. That is 'chess,' not 'chest,' pie."

articles.title: Royal Navy warships and helicopter track Russian vessels in three-day operation
articles.summary: HMS Duncan, HMS St Albans and HMS Severn used radars to monitor four vessels as they passed through the North Sea and English Channel last week.
articles.body:
Royal Navy warships and a helicopter spent three days tracking Russian Navy vessels and sanctioned cargo ships in an "intense" operation in the North Sea and English Channel.

HMS Duncan, HMS St Albans and HMS Severn used radars to monitor four vessels last week, while a Merlin helicopter provided surveillance from the sky.

"Since that successful operation, we have seen Russian shadow fleet vessels increasingly forced to change their routes, imposing significant cost and delays to their journeys," Gen Sir Gwyn Jenkins, the First Sea Lord and Chief of Naval Staff, said.

It comes as data shows Royal Navy activity to monitor Russian movements is up 25% so far this year compared to 2025.

During the August operation, the Royal Navy warships including a Type 45 destroyer and a Type 23 frigate, tracked Russian destroyer Admiral Levchenko as it escorted sanctioned cargo vessels General Skobelev and Sparta south through the North Sea and into the English Channel.

The Royal Navy said Russia was "forced" to respond with "costly military resources" including the frigate Neustrashimy.

A statement said a Nato ally then took over monitoring off the coast of France, without specifying the country.

The operation comes after Royal Marine Commandos boarded a Russian "shadow fleet" oil tanker in the English Channel in June .

Marines joined by National Crime Agency (NCA) officers, with the support of the RAF, intercepted and boarded the Smyrtos in a six-hour operation - the first of its kind by UK armed forces.

NCA officers arrested an Indian national, 38, on suspicion of sanctions offences under the Russia Regulations and he was taken into custody.

The UK has sanctioned more than 500 vessels it says are part of Russia's so-called shadow fleet.

Oil and gas revenue as a percentage of the total Russian budget fell to just 23% in 2025, the lowest percentage share in the past 20 years, according to an analysis by the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies.

However the institute notes that was compensated by strong growth from other taxes, namely a hike in VAT and corporate profits tax.

Moscow has also benefited from a recent rise in oil prices following the Iran war, however the broader economy is slowing.

articles.title: Mumby motoring memorabilia museum's 'last lap' for charity funds
articles.summary: On Your Marques Model Car Museum in Mumby is reopening for the last time over the bank holiday weekend.
articles.body:
A closed motorsport memorabilia museum is reopening over the August bank holiday weekend for a "last lap" to raise money for charity.

The family-run On Your Marques Model Car Museum in Mumby, Lincolnshire, has been closed since 2023 due to the owners' ill health.

The museum is reopening from 10:00 until 16:00 BST on Saturday, Sunday and Monday to raise funds for the National Brain Appeal's Dementia Research Fund.

Created by Jane and Chris Dring, the museum houses more than 1,200 model cars and motorsport items, plus a cafe and a four-lane Scalextric circuit.

Jane passed away "unexpectedly" in 2012, the museum said, with Chris recently suffering from ill health.

Motoring journalist Steve Fowler said: "This is On Your Marques' last lap and we want it packed with people, laughter and Scalextric racing."

Steve, who is Jane and Chris' nephew, and other relatives are helping to reopen the museum over the weekend.

"I think Chris has got about 18,000 models in total," Fowler said, explaining that some are held in storage.

"He got his first model as an eight year old, that's on display.

"Everything from Formula One, Matchbox, Scalextric, his model planes, model motorbikes."

Steve said his uncle's childhood hobby grew so big over the years that he decided to turn it into a museum.

Discussing the 30ft Scalextric set, he said: "It's brilliant - you can spend hours on it.

"There's four lanes, so you can come down with a family and all grab a controller each.

"We've got a little timing board and you can get the quickest lap."

Steve said he would love people to visit to see the collection one final time.

"Come for the cars, stay for the Scalextric and cake, and help us support a brilliant cause," he added.

articles.body: Vroom vroom, Donald Trump revved up his engine as he made “a little circle in a nice, secure…slightly slower” presidential limo the Beast, before kicking off the Freedom 250 Grand Prix in the nation’s capital.Then the POTUS waved a big green flag fast and furious like an excited schoolboy to let a bunch of fast, flashy cars go swooshing around a 1.7-mile street circuit at 200 mph in 147 laps covering roughly 250 miles.The earth trembled. But mercifully none of the more than 200 manhole covers welded down around the course flew off. Carefully shielded by their nervous curators, thousands of artefacts in the museums along the route too survived as “the beautiful cars” made freedom go “roaring like never before.”Sunday’s picnic marked the end of Trump’s “Summer of fun” for America’s 250th big birthday bash, suggested the New York Times, with several events with a Trumpian flavor — from a UFC fight on the White House lawn to a massive July Fourth fireworks show on the National Mall.Whoa whoa, not so fast, not so soon. There were more shake downs to do. More memes to mash. And more enemies to bash. So America’s own all-in-one Swiss knife let loose a fresh salvo of verbal missiles at the enemy — No, not Iran but Canada.As trade talks with its neighbor collapsed, Trump calling it “difficult and unreasonable” and its negotiators “clowns,” slapped punitive 50% tariffs with a threat to change the name of Lake Ontario to ‘Lake America’ with a new LEGO map on Truth Social.Though shaken, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney chose to do what no other major U.S. ally has done, hitting back with tariffs on steel products and a swath of new duties on $20-billion worth of U.S. products exported to Canada.But undeterred by the prospect of toilet roll prices hitting the fan, Trump followed up the threat with an executive order making the change official.“We have a gulf and we have a lake – now all we need is an ocean. Maybe we’ll have to change the name of the Atlantic and/or the Pacific,” he declared, “Maybe we’ll change them both.”“As you know, Canada has been ripping us off for a long time on trade. Sad,” said Trump who had previously renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America” on the first day of his second term in office.“Even the military: we defend Canada for nothing. We don’t get anything. They don’t pay us to defend Canada. But we defend Canada,” Trump complained.And as his expletive-laden “Operation Epic Fury” failed to tame Iran even after six months, Trump “unleashed” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, as the Wall Street Journal put it, to redouble economic pressure on Tehran and its enablers.“Our objective is to sever every economic lifeline that sustains this tyrannical regime until Tehran stands alone,” said Bessent announcing a rather prosaically named “Operation Economic Outcast,” comparing it to D-Day.Trump is working the phones and “every country has a defined timeline to shut down activities we have identified,” he said, “If they do not take action, we will do so unilaterally.” But he declined to lay out the timelines or name names.Trump then despatched CIA director John Ratcliffe on a widely publicised “very sort of semi-routine” secretive visit to Moscow to share the agency’s bleak assessment of the Russian war against Ukraine, and urge Moscow to cut a deal.Some officials cited by the New York Times hoped that President Vladimir Putin, a former intelligence officer himself, would see a message from the CIA director as more urgent and credible than communications through normal diplomatic channels.“We would like to see the war with Ukraine end,” Trump himself told Fox News. “Now something may come out of it. We’re working very hard to get that war ended and frankly they both want to see it ended at this point.”Before Ratcliffe flew to Moscow, US intelligence indicated that the Kremlin views the Iran war as an opportunity to escalate action against US interests, according to a Washington Post report.With just 67 days to go before the crucial midterm elections, US Citizenship and Immigration Services has reassigned hundreds of fraud detection officers to look for noncitizens in voter registration data, according to another Post report.Immigration arrests too have hit record highs with ICE increasingly targeting people with no criminal record to get closer than ever to meeting its goal of 2,000 daily arrests.Meanwhile, miffed at a judge’s order to remove Trump’s name from the facade of the Kennedy Center of Performing Arts, government lawyers argued that it may have to be demolished without Trump’s planned renovations and addition of his name as its ‘restorer.’Not so fast, said the judge peppering the arts institution lawyers with inconvenient questions about the urgency of adding Trump’s name to the building by Sept. 8 and if it wouldn’t amount to promoting a specific individual. But he did postpone a final decision for a month to keep the pot boiling.Meanwhile, a coalition of more than 600 preservation groups, architectural associations and Tribal governments have sought lawmakers’ intervention to check moves to loosen rules that govern proposed changes to historic landmarks and Indian tribal sites.But away from the prying eyes of nosy judges, the US Embassy in the Dominican Republic reportedly wants to get rid of a recently removed “woke” painting by celebrated artist Kehinde Wiley, who painted Barack Obama’s presidential portrait.— Probably to replace it with one big beautiful portrait trumpeting Trump!(By arrangement with The American Bazaar)Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Gaza farmer returns to the grapevines he couldn’t bear to abandon
articles.summary: After nearly three years of war, a farmer returns to Sheikh Ijlin’s renowned grape fields.
articles.body:
Gaza City, Gaza Strip - It's 4am, and Gaza is still dark and quiet. But Khaled Abu Madeen has a routine, one that he has recently picked up again after being forced to abandon it over nearly three years of war.

He walks between the rows of grapevines in Sheikh Ijlin, in the southwestern corner of Gaza City, alongside his workers, checking the fruit and cutting bunches from the vines that have survived Israel's genocidal war.

The early morning air is cooler. The first light begins to spread across the vineyard, revealing rows of green that, for a time, Khaled feared he might never see again.

For Khaled, who is 50, this year is more than a harvest. It is the return of a life he thought he had lost.

“I feel like I have returned to my soul,” he says, as he works among the vines.

His family has cultivated grapes and figs in Sheikh Ijlin for generations. The land was inherited from his father and grandfather, and Khaled eventually made farming his full-time profession, leaving behind a career in project management.

Then, in October 2023, the war began. Khaled had the opportunity to leave. His wife is Lebanese-Italian, and Khaled himself had previously studied in Italy, earning an undergraduate and a postgraduate degree.

Moving to safety in Italy made sense. But that would mean abandoning his vineyards, and Khaled couldn't do it.

For the first few months of the war, Khaled stayed in Gaza City, refusing to leave despite the danger.

His wife and children were eventually evacuated to Italy. Khaled stayed behind, trying to remain close to the land and his elderly mother.

Then the Israeli strikes moved closer. He says he received a call ordering him to leave immediately, with a threat that the house would be bombed if he did not.

"I had no choice," Khaled recounts. "I left with my mother and fled to Deir el-Balah, in central Gaza."

Away from his vineyards, Khaled says, his thoughts remained fixed on what was happening to his land.

Despite the great danger - northern Gaza, including Gaza City, has been devastated by Israeli forces in the war - he tried more than once to get back.

During one attempt, he went with two workers to check the fields. Israeli forces opened fire, he says, injuring one of the workers.

“We ran away from the shooting,” Khaled recalls. “We stayed for hours until we were able to rescue him after he had lost a lot of blood.”

And yet, despite that experience, Khaled couldn't get the thought out of his head: He had to return to his vines.

articles.title: 'Soldiers attempted mutiny': Niger's defence minister after gunfire, blasts heard in capital Niamey
articles.summary: Rest of World News: The Niger government said a group of soldiers had attempted to stage a mutiny and that the situation was now under control after sustained gunfire and.
articles.body: The Niger government said a group of soldiers had attempted to stage a mutiny and that the situation was now under control after sustained gunfire and explosions were heard overnight into Saturday in Niamey, the capital of the West African country.According to defence minister General Salifou Mody, the soldiers took several officers hostage at Niamey’s Diori Hamani International Airport, which houses a key military air base known as Base 101, as well as in the Plateau administrative district, home to the presidential palace and other key institutions.Mody described the alleged mutiny attempt as a “break with discipline and military regulations.”As the attack unfolded, state broadcaster RTN halted its live transmission for several hours before resuming its broadcast.The incident marked the third attack this year on the international airport, following two earlier assaults by jihadi rebels. Besides Niger’s air force Base 101, the airport also houses the headquarters of a joint military force comprising Niger, Burkina Faso and Mali.Niger has been ruled by a military junta since a 2023 coup that brought Abdourahamane Tchiani to power. Under the junta, the country has severed ties with long-time Western security partners and turned to Russia. It continues to face attacks by jihadi rebels and worsening economic hardship following cuts in aid.The ruling military council, known as the National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland, called for unity. “Our defence and security forces are mobilised for the Defence of the Fatherland. Let us remain united, vigilant and supportive,” it said in a Facebook post.The latest attack adds to pressure on the National Council, which has struggled to contain deadly jihadi violence that has battered parts of Africa’s Sahel region, including neighbouring Burkina Faso and Mali, which are also governed by military juntas.(With AP inputs)Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Israeli settlers surround Palestinian home in occupied West Bank’s Qusra
articles.summary: At least four people trapped inside their home, as earlier siege on Palestinian families has continued for three weeks.
articles.body:
Israeli settlers, backed by Israeli forces, have surrounded a Palestinian home in the village of Qusra , south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank.

At least four Palestinians were trapped inside the home on Saturday while settlers set fire to nearby land, according to Al Jazeera journalists. Coordination is under way to allow ambulances to reach the area and evacuate one injured person.

Qusra has faced an escalating campaign of Israeli settler violence over the past month.

Since August 9, settlers have besieged three Palestinian homes in the Ras al-Ain area, trapping families inside and cutting access to water, electricity and other essential supplies. Settlers also set fire to a mosque in the village in July.

“We’re not safe here. We fear for our own safety. Settlers are still moving freely around the house and attack the residents of the nearby houses too,” Loui Abu Ridi, one resident who has been trapped inside his home for weeks, told Al Jazeera. “We’re trying to get more basic supplies, and we have elderly and children.”

Palestinian journalist Sara Abu al-Rob, reporting from Ramallah on Saturday, told Al Jazeera that Israeli soldiers and settlers attacked six Palestinians in the village who were trying to install metal bars and window shields on their homes to protect their families, adding that “Israeli settlers keep throwing stones and flaming material onto the houses there.”

She said one of those besieged, Loai al-Bairoty, was injured earlier in the day, and that residents told her “the Israeli army is protecting the settlers, not the residents who are trying to reach their lands”.

Qusra Mayor Abdel Azim Wadi told Al Jazeera that Israeli forces at the scene had instead attempted to arrest the besieged Palestinians themselves.

Israeli forces have declared the area a closed military zone and restricted Palestinians from entering and leaving, placing a gate at the main entrance of Qusra itself. Palestinians travelling into the village are forced to take alternative routes, which are often blocked by Israeli forces.

Abu Ridi told Al Jazeera the feeling of being trapped is “a nightmare … 21 days, we can’t even sleep, we have to stay up at night [and] keep watching the security cameras, because those settlers can attack any time”.

He said residents have to coordinate with the mayor of Qusra to get food and supplies, and it can take three to four days to get approval. “We’re not allowed to live freely in and out of our houses,” he added.

On Wednesday, the Israeli military erected three new roadblocks at locations that encircled the top of the Ras al-Ain hill, disconnecting homes from the area below.

In a statement on Saturday, the Israeli military said it had responded to reports of “violent clashes” involving “Israeli rioters” in Qusra, removing them from the home and confiscating their vehicles.

It said forces would remain in the area “to prevent further disturbances and restore order”.

Settler attacks – supported or overlooked by the Israeli military – on Palestinian homes, businesses and farmland across the West Bank have been common for decades as illegal settlements have expanded across the territory.

The attacks have increased in intensity and frequency since Israel launched its genocidal war against Palestinians in Gaza in October 2023, in response to the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel.

articles.title: AEW All In 2026 match card, preview and predictions
articles.summary: Kenny Omega defends the AEW World Championship against Will Ospreay in the main event at Wembley Stadium, headlining a stacked AEW All In card.
articles.body: All Elite Wrestling (AEW) will hold its biggest event of the year at Wembley Stadium in London on Sunday. All In has proven to be a showcase of some of the pro wrestling’s best. This year will be no different with championship matches up and down the card, including the AEW World Championship being on the line between Kenny Omega and Will Ospreay. All In has also featured some surprises in the past with massive returns and debuts that have shaped the AEW roster. Read below for a list of the match card, a preview and predictions for how All In will shake out. COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK == Adam Page, Bandido & Brody King (c) vs. Jay White, Austin Gunn & Colten Gunn vs. Orange Cassidy, Kyle O’Reilly and Roderick Strong vs. Claudio Castagnoli, Pac & Wheeler Yuta vs. Ricochet, Bishop Kaun & Toa Liona vs. David Finlay, Clark Connors & Gabe Kidd vs. Wildcard Team for the AEW World Trios Championship A major trios match will kick off the two-hour All In Buy In and bleed into the first few minutes of All In. Adam Page and Brodido, the Bang Bang Gang, The Conglomeration, the Death Riders, The Demand and The Dogs will compete for the AEW World Trios Championship. But there is a wildcard entrant in this match. It could be anyone or it could be who we’re all expecting it to be. All In has been full of surprises in recent years. Let’s get another one in to start the show off with a bang. Prediction: Adam Page and Brodido retain the trios title despite the chaos that will ensue. == Kyle Fletcher (c) vs. Konosuke Takeshita vs. Kazuchika Okada for the AEW International Championship Kyle Fletcher, Konosuke Takeshita and Kazuchika Okada may be three of the best professional wrestlers in the world. Their rivalry began after Takeshita defeated Okada for the AEW International Championship at Double or Nothing. Fletcher returned and turned on Takeshita. Weeks later, Fletcher won the title at Dynamite: Spring Breakin’ and turned the title picture on its head. Now, the three men will meet at All In. And while it may seem like Fletcher and Okada are on the same page, with the title on the line, it’ll be every man for himself. Prediction: Kyle Fletcher, somehow, pulls it out and retains the title. == Kevin Knight (c) vs. Darby Allin for the AEW TNT Championship Kevin Knight has been the TNT champion for more than 135 days after winning a 10-man Casino Gauntlet match in Vancouver back in April. He’s gone from a fan favorite to the most hated after he turned on "Speedball" Mike Bailey and aligned himself, loosely, with the Don Callis Family. He’s been one of the top stars on the AEW roster since then but may have feuded with the wrong guy in Darby Allin. The challenger has proven that he’s willing to go above and beyond to win any match – even without gold on the line. Allin has been back in the fray for some gold since losing his AEW world title at Double or Nothing to MJF. As he’s dealt with Knight’s mind games, Allin has still shown he’s not willing to go down easy. This will be a big matchup. Prediction: Darby Allin ends Knight’s title reign. == Megan Bayne and Lena Kross (c) vs. Alex Windsor and Jamie Hayter for the AEW Women’s World Tag Team Championship Megan Bayne and Lena Kross, the Divine Dominion have been at the top of the AEW women’s tag team division since March and have dispatched every opponent who have come their way. The Brawling Birds, Alex Windsor and Jamie Hayter, have been two women who have not backed down from challenging Bayne and Kross. The Brawling Birds have their home country behind them in this match and the momentum may carry over for them to get the win. Prediction: The Brawling Birds take home the gold. == Jon Moxley (c) vs. Nigel McGuiness for the AEW Continental Championship It has been a long and grueling Continental Challenge Cup and the finals will see continental champion Jon Moxley defend his title against Nigel McGuiness. Moxley is back on the All In card after losing the AEW World Championship to Adam Page last year. Moxley is looking for his own personal redemption and it may come at the expense of Nigel McGuiness, who is already battling an injury. McGuiness’ in-ring appearances have been few and far between but getting back in shape to make it through to the end is an accomplishment in and of itself. I don’t think Moxley can afford to lose this match. Prediction: Moxley retains the AEW Continental Championship. == Men’s Casino Gauntlet match The men’s Casino Gauntlet match will have a title shot waiting for the winner. The match has seen its own share of surprises in the past and this one may not be different. We already know who the initial entrants are: Andrade El Idolo, MJF, Tommaso Ciampa, Mark Davis and Chris Jericho. Nobody knows who else is going to be in this match, which could make for some wild in-ring action. MJF has the edge after winning this match last year at All In. Will he be able to pull it off again or is his focus too much on AEW national champion Andrade? Prediction: It’s a wild one. Somehow, Chris Jericho sneaks away with the victory. == Willow Nightingale (c) vs. Mercedes Moné for the AEW Women’s World Championship Mercedes Moné has been lusting to get back on top of the AEW women’s division since her return to the ring earlier this year. She won the Owen Hart Foundation Women’s Tournament to earn a shot at the AEW Women’s World Championship. After Willow Nightingale defeated Thekla at Redemption, the match at All In became more about the history between Moné and Nightingale than just the championship. Nightingale was the fourth-ever AEW TBS champion and held the belt for 35 days before Moné ended her first reign. Moné held that title for 584 days before Nightingale finally got her revenge. Nightingale was forced to give up her title due to an injury but made her way back to capture the AEW Women’s World Championship. Now, Moné is on her radar again and apparently delivered an on-screen hand injury to Nightingale on the final "Dynamite" before All In. Prediction: Mercedes Moné picks up the title win. == Christian Cage and Adam Copeland (c) vs. Matt Jackson and Nick Jackson for the AEW World Tag Team Championship The temps between the teams of Christian Cage and Adam Copeland and Matt and Nick Jackson have turned up ever since they teamed up at Grand Slam Mexico. Things between the teams got even more chaotic on "Dynamite" as Copeland was the last one standing when they butted heads. The AEW world tag titles have meant the world to have for Cope and Cage. But the Young Bucks have been a dominant force in tag team wrestling for years. It’s a fairly important matchup for the wrestling industry and it will be a treat to see these four men in the ring, going up against each other, at the same time. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS Prediction: Cope and Cage retain in a great tag match. == Kenny Omega (c) vs. Will Ospreay for the AEW World Championship It’s the match everyone is waiting for: Kenny Omega vs. Will Ospreay for the AEW World Championship. I don’t have to write too much on their history. Anyone who has ever watched pro wrestling knows the epic matches they put on in New Japan – some of the best matches in wrestling history. Both competitors are a little older now, and a little wiser. Omega is on top of the division as the champion after beating MJF at Spring Breakin’. Ospreay won the Owen Hart Foundation Men’s Tournament to earn the title shot, which everyone initially thought was going to be against MJF. But now Ospreay has a chance to dethrone his "hero" in Omega and do it in the main event at Wembley Stadium in his home country. Ospreay has been clear that it has always been his dream to be the focal point at Wembley and now he can be that and more. Prediction: It is Will Ospreay’s time. Ospreay wins in a massive main event. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP == How to watch AEW All In begins at 1 p.m. ET and can be purchased in the United States on HBO Max, Amazon Prime, DAZN, PPV.com, YouTube, DirecTV, Sling and Dish Network. The Buy In begins at 11 a.m. ET.

articles.title: 'Resolve, harmony, dialogue': Images of RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat light up Times Square ahead of US event
articles.summary: US News: Images of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat were displayed on billboards in New York’s Times Square ahead of his scheduled address.
articles.body: Images of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat were displayed on billboards in New York’s Times Square ahead of his scheduled address to members of the Indian diaspora at Madison Square Garden.Images of Bhagwat bearing the words “Resolve, Harmony and Dialogue” were projected on one of the main billboards at New York’s Times Square on Friday evening.In the US, Bhagwat is scheduled to address a gathering of around 5,000 people at the iconic Madison Square Garden on Saturday.The event, titled ‘Universal Oneness Celebration’, is being organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue (AHEAD), which has described it as a “landmark Raksha Bandhan gathering”.The organisers said the event will explore the theme of universal oneness through cultural presentations and keynote addresses, drawing on the Hindu principle of ‘Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam’, which means “the world is one family”.New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani said he does not support the planned Madison Square Garden event featuring Bhagwat, but acknowledged that the city may not have the authority to cancel the “private” gathering.Earlier during his ongoing US tour, Bhagwat visited the ISKCON temple in New York, where he took part in a food distribution initiative for homeless people and spoke about the role of Krishna consciousness in addressing conflicts and divisions.Bhagwat visited the temple at 26 Second Avenue, where the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (ISKCON) was founded in 1966.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Union ministers Chirag Paswan, Jitan Ram Manjhi clash over quotas, demand each other's resignation
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Two cabinet ministers - Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi - in the Narendra Modi-led government sparred over the issue of reservation on S.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Two cabinet ministers - Chirag Paswan and Jitan Ram Manjhi - in the Narendra Modi-led government sparred over the issue of reservation on Saturday and sought each other's resignation.The controversy began after Hindustani Awam Morcha (Secular) president and Union minister Jitan Ram Manjhi's son, Santosh Kumar Suman, sought a review of the quota policy, backing the sub-categorisation of the Scheduled Castes (SCs) and the Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the reservation regime.“I think the purpose of reservation has not been served. The concept of creating the Mahadalit category with 18 of the 22 Dalit caste groups has been defeated due to the wide gap among the beneficiaries. The Extremely Backward Classes (EBC) category was created out of the other backward castes (OBCs), and the same was true for the concept of economically weaker sections (EWS) among the upper castes,” Suman had said.“How can it be wrong to ask which sections have benefited from reservation and to what extent, and which people standing at the very bottom of the social ladder remain deprived of it? Why is no DM or SP from the Musahar community, which has 4 percent population in Bihar? A comparative study is needed. Why will one section get 8 percent and another 80 percent among the beneficiaries?” he added.Chirag counters HAMThe remarks, however, did not sit well with another NDA ally, Chirag Paswan. The Union minister of food processing industries said that if Manjhi and his son want sub-quotas and a creamy layer within SC reservation, then the Union minister should resign."People ask, 'Why isn't there a 'creamy layer' provision?' Well, let them give it up, then - let them stop availing the benefits of reservation," Chirag said."If Jitan Ram Manjhi feels these measures should be implemented, should he not resign first? Let him introduce the 'creamy layer' concept - after all, he would fall under that category too, wouldn't he? He should resign, and his son - who is present here - should resign as well," he added.He also asserted that the basis of reservation lies in social factors and discussing it from an economic perspective "goes against the Constitution.""The basis is social - specifically, the issue of untouchability within society," he said.How Manjhi respondedLater in the day, Jitan Ram Manjhi slammed his cabinet colleague, accusing him of not caring about poor people."People will end up being deprived of the benefits of reservation because of this stance. However, we maintain that this division is essential in the broader public interest."Since he (Chirag) does not want to look after the interests of our poor people, he should resign," he added.SC-ST quota rowThe controversy stems from a 2024 Supreme Court judgment that allowed states to sub-classify Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) to ensure that the benefits of reservation reach the more backward groups within these categories.It also asked governments to devise suitable criteria to bar the ‘creamy layer’ among SCs and STs from availing reservation.The Centre, however, told the Supreme Court in an affidavit that the creamy layer principle cannot be extended to SCs and STs. It said the principle currently applies only to Other Backward Classes (OBCs)."It has nowhere specifically been held that the principle of creamy layer is applicable to SCs and STs. The reference made to the concept of creamy layer… appears to be the general observation with regard to reservation in respect of OBCs (Other Backward Classes)/SEBCs (Socially and Educationally Backward Classes)."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Diane Keaton’s former Beverly Hills home, the 8,434-square-foot Spanish Colonial estate, gets contingent offer after $6.5 million price cut from $25 million to $18.5 million
articles.summary: Real Estate News: Diane Keaton’s former Beverly Hills home has come under contingent offer nearly a year after it first hit the market for $25 million. The late actress.
articles.body: Diane Keaton’s former Beverly Hills home has come under contingent offer nearly a year after it first hit the market for $25 million. The late actress’ sprawling Spanish Colonial-style estate was most recently asking $18.5 million, after enduring multiple price cuts and repeated stints on and off the market. According to Realtor.com, the property’s listing has now been updated to reflect the contingent offer, although the final offer price and terms have not been disclosed.Diane Keaton’s Beverly Hills home is under contingent offerThe 8,434-square-foot Beverly Hills residence, once owned and renovated by Oscar-winning actress Diane Keaton, has taken a lengthy journey through the luxury real estate market.The property was initially listed in October 2025 for $25 million, less than two weeks after Keaton died from bacterial pneumonia at the age of 79. Since then, the six-bedroom, nine-bathroom home has repeatedly gone on and off the market, accompanied by several reductions in its asking price.The estate was relisted at $19.5 million in May 2026, before another price cut in July brought the asking price down to $18.5 million.That latest reduction may have finally attracted a serious buyer. Realtor.com reported on August 27 that the listing had been updated to show the property under contingent offer. The specific value and conditions of the offer remain undisclosed.The current listing is being represented by Rayni Williams and Branden Williams of The Beverly Hills Estates, according to real-estate industry data.The celebrity home once belonged to MadonnaKeaton purchased the Beverly Hills property for $8.1 million in 2007, taking ownership after pop icon Madonna. Keaton lived in the house from 2007 until 2010 and carried out an extensive renovation that transformed the residence while preserving much of its historic character.The property's celebrity history did not end with Keaton. Following her ownership, the residence was also associated with Ryan Murphy, the creator of American Horror Story.The Beverly Hills Flats estate has also been featured in Architectural Digest, highlighting the architectural and design significance of the property.For Keaton, however, the house was more than another luxury residence. It was another opportunity to indulge her longstanding passion for architecture, restoration and interiors.Diane Keaton’s design influence remains throughout the houseVisitors entering the property are immediately confronted with Keaton’s distinctive design sensibility.Listing agent Rayni Williams previously described the foyer to the New York Post as a library and seating area where Keaton’s personality remains particularly apparent.“You walk into the foyer, which is a library with seating area, and you’re really enveloped in Diane’s energy because it greets you and that’s untouched,” Williams said.Williams also highlighted Keaton’s love of books and reading, saying that visitors could still feel the actress’ “heart and soul” in the space.That connection is particularly fitting given Keaton’s reputation as an architecture and design enthusiast. Her approach to her homes was rarely about simply modernizing a property. Instead, she often sought to preserve its history while giving it a distinctive personal character.Inside the 8,434-square-foot Spanish Colonial homeThe Beverly Hills residence was originally designed by celebrated architect Ralph Flewelling and retains numerous details associated with its Spanish Colonial architectural heritage.Among the property's defining features are dark wood ceiling beams, arched doorways, terra-cotta floors, wrought-iron accents and rustic fireplaces.The result is a home that feels both historic and highly personal, with Keaton’s renovation choices still evident throughout much of the residence.Natural light plays a major role in the interiors, while darker wood and architectural elements provide contrast. The combination gives the expansive house a sense of warmth rather than allowing its size to make the rooms feel impersonal.Several of the bedrooms feature fireplaces, while the office includes exposed beams and a tiled fireplace, reinforcing the property's Spanish-inspired character.A formal dining room opens to the courtyardThe home was designed with entertaining in mind, offering multiple spaces where residents can host guests.The formal dining room features warm Spanish-inspired light fixtures and a wall of French doors that open directly onto a courtyard.The connection between the indoor and outdoor spaces is one of the property's defining characteristics, with the courtyard providing an intimate extension of the main living areas.The kitchen similarly blends old-world architectural influences with a lighter farmhouse-inspired aesthetic. It features a dedicated dining area as well as space for a lounge, creating a more casual gathering spot within the otherwise grand residence.The backyard feels like a private resortOutside, the Beverly Hills estate becomes even more expansive.A tree-lined courtyard and Spanish-style fountain create a secluded setting, while the backyard features a pool and spa, guesthouse and sport court.The combination effectively turns the property into a private resort, offering spaces for both relaxation and entertaining.The guesthouse adds another layer of privacy and flexibility, while the landscaped grounds provide a peaceful contrast to the highly sought-after Beverly Hills location.Realtor says Diane Keaton had a rare design aestheticFor Rayni Williams, Keaton’s contribution to the property is what makes it particularly distinctive.“Diane was one of the most prolific architectural and design minds that we’ve ever seen in the real estate community,” Williams said.“There are only a very small handful of people that had her aesthetic.”That assessment helps explain why the property has attracted attention beyond its price tag. It is not simply a celebrity-owned Beverly Hills mansion; it is a residence that still carries the visual imprint of one of Hollywood’s best-known architecture and design enthusiasts.The $6.5 million price reductionThe journey from $25 million to $18.5 million represents a $6.5 million reduction in the property's asking price—roughly 26% below its original listing price.The property was initially placed on the market at $25 million in October 2025. After several attempts to find a buyer, the asking price was reduced to $19.5 million in May 2026.The final reduction to $18.5 million came in July.Within weeks, the listing moved into contingent-offer status.While the offer does not necessarily mean the transaction is complete, it represents a significant development for a property that had spent months searching for a buyer.Diane Keaton’s other iconic Los Angeles home sold for $18 millionThe Beverly Hills property is not the only Diane Keaton residence to make headlines following her death.On August 18, 2026, the actress’ final Los Angeles home in Sullivan Canyon sold for $18 million.Known affectionately as “The House That Pinterest Built,” the property became closely associated with Keaton’s passion for renovation and design. She documented the transformation in her 2017 book of the same name.Keaton bought the Sullivan Canyon property for $4.7 million in 2011 and spent years turning it into her dream home. She ultimately listed it for sale in March 2025, months before her death.The residence was characterized by abundant natural light, large windows and open-concept rooms combining neutral interiors with more playful artistic touches.The listing described it as a residence that balanced history, craftsmanship and modern comfort, calling it the “final architectural statement” of a design icon.‘The House That Pinterest Built’ reflected Keaton’s design philosophyKeaton’s Sullivan Canyon home was arguably the clearest expression of her approach to residential architecture.Rather than treating a house as simply a luxury asset, she approached renovation as a creative project. The property took years to develop and became an extension of her personality.She once described the home affectionately, saying, “Something’s right, because I love it,” while explaining that it was the first of her many design projects that felt like a forever home.The sale of that residence for $18 million means another significant piece of Keaton’s real-estate legacy has already passed to a new owner.Now her former Beverly Hills estate could be heading toward the same fate.Diane Keaton’s Beverly Hills legacy lives onIf the contingent offer ultimately progresses to a completed sale, the Beverly Hills property will mark another chapter in the dispersal of Keaton’s personal real-estate legacy.Yet the house’s most distinctive quality is likely to remain: the design decisions made by Keaton herself.From its Spanish Colonial details and dark wood beams to its terra-cotta floors, arched doorways, courtyard and resort-style backyard, the property retains the aesthetic that made it unmistakably hers.For now, the $18.5 million contingent offer represents a potential turning point for the historic Beverly Hills residence.After starting at $25 million and undergoing a $6.5 million price reduction, Diane Keaton’s former home may finally be on its way to a new owner, while preserving the design legacy of the actress who once called it home.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.summary: Rest of World News: A violent Haitian gang has released 13 hostages — seven women and six children — from among 50 people it kidnapped nearly a week ago when it launched .
articles.body: A violent Haitian gang has released 13 hostages — seven women and six children — from among 50 people it kidnapped nearly a week ago when it launched a deadly attack on a farming community near the capital, Port-au-Prince.Unicef, the United Nations’ children’s agency that helped secure their release, said late Friday that those freed included three children under the age of two, a seven-year-old child, and two teenage girls.According to Unicef, it worked with leaders of Kenscoff, the targeted farming settlement, to help secure the release of the women and children. It was not immediately clear whether they needed medical treatment or whether more women and children remained in captivity.“This release offers a rare moment of hope amid the violence threatening children in Haiti. The Kenscoff abduction was not an isolated incident but another stark reminder of the scale and frequency of attacks on children across the country,” Yannig Dussart, Unicef’s deputy representative in the Caribbean nation, told The Associated Press.Gangs killed at least 47 people during the August 23 attack on Kenscoff, a once-peaceful farming community in the hills above Port-au-Prince.A gang leader known as Izo 2 had threatened to execute all the hostages if police killed any gang members during their efforts to secure the abductees. Izo 2 leads an armed group in the area on behalf of, and in coordination with, other gang leaders, including Izo, who is considered one of Haiti’s most powerful gang leaders.UN estimates show that attacks in Kenscoff over two months in early 2025 killed more than 260 people and resulted in the destruction or burning of 200 homes. Around 3,000 people were forced to flee. Nearly a dozen further attacks have occurred since then, involving rape, kidnapping, arson and livestock theft.The neighbourhood overlooks routes leading to Petion-Ville, where several embassies, upscale hotels and the temporary seat of government are located. It also overlooks a major road connecting the capital with southern Haiti.While individual kidnappings are commonplace in Haiti, mass abductions are less common. articles.title: After Bombay HC rap, FDA withdraws orders against Cipla, MCA eateries
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Saturday withdrew two enforcement orders after the Bombay high court pulled up the regul.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) on Saturday withdrew two enforcement orders after the Bombay high court pulled up the regulator over its handling of separate cases involving five MCA eateries and a Cipla facility in Pune.The court's observations came while hearing two matters — one concerning five restaurants at the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) premises in Bandra-Kurla Complex and the other involving Cipla Pharma & Life Sciences Ltd's facility in Pune.FDA withdraws action against MCA eateriesIn the MCA matter, the FDA told the court that it would withdraw its order suspending the operations of five restaurants after the bench warned of contempt action against the officials concerned.A fresh inspection found that the restaurants were 88 per cent compliant with food safety rules, the bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad noted.The eateries, however, faced a separate licensing issue as they were being operated by M/s Shirke Infrastructure, while the licences were issued in the name of the MCA.The court said there was no provision under the law prohibiting such an arrangement. It also reminded the FDA that, at the previous hearing, it had specifically directed officials to apply their mind to the issue and take a pragmatic view."However, despite clearly saying this, the FDA has disobeyed our order and taken a pedantic view instead of a pragmatic view. We are tired of scolding the department and officers all the time. It is now time to pass stinging orders. We will issue contempt action against the concerned officers. Let them convince us or go to jail," the HC said.Following the court's warning, the FDA agreed to issue a fresh notice to the MCA, hear its response on the contract with Shirke Infrastructure and pass a reasoned order.The court accepted the undertaking and said that since the restaurants were now compliant with food safety rules, the suspension order stood vacated. The eateries could therefore reopen.The bench also questioned the FDA's repeated "undue haste" in passing orders without properly examining the law."How many times should we try to convince and balance equities so that the department does not feel discouraged? Why do we say don't kill a mosquito with a sword? Do you feel you are a lord and you can do anything?" the HC questioned.FDA withdraws Cipla licence cancellationIn the second matter, the court questioned the FDA's decision to cancel the drug sale licences of Cipla Pharma & Life Sciences Ltd's facility in Pune. The regulator subsequently withdrew the cancellation order after the bench criticised the procedure it had followed.The court particularly questioned an FDA email asking a company representative to appear for a hearing on a public holiday declared by the state government."You (FDA) are doing a laudable and appreciative job, but now you are going overboard. This is not the first time this is happening. You have wronged, and now you have to resolve the issue," the bench said.The court said the FDA had acted in a "high-handed" manner and followed an improper procedure while cancelling the licence."The order is against the principles of natural justice," the high court said.The FDA had cancelled the drug sale licences of Cipla Pharma & Life Sciences Ltd's carrying and forwarding facility at Wadki in Pune after alleged violations were found during a follow-up investigation into the packaging and recall of Reactin Plus tablets.The cancellation order had come into effect from August 27 before the High Court's intervention led the regulator to withdraw it.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.summary: Nepal's flood and mudslide death toll reaches more than 670 with nearly 3,000 missing as rain and fog halt search and rescue operations in the disaster zone.
articles.body: The death toll from the devastating floods and mudslides along the Nepal-China border has risen to at least 676 people, as rescue operations stall amid poor weather. After Nepali authorities updated their figures Saturday, the combined toll in Nepal and Tibet rose to 676 dead and nearly 3,000 people missing, according to The Associated Press. Chinese authorities have reported seven deaths and more than 550 missing, while Nepal’s disaster agency said the death toll had climbed to 669 with 2,426 people missing. Experts believe Wednesday's mudslides and flash flooding across Nepal and China's Tibet region were caused by a large chunk of ice breaking off a glacier and falling into the Lhende Khola River. Rescue operations at the main disaster zone have been complicated by damaged roads and difficulty establishing communication, and look only to get more difficult, as intermittent rain is expected through the weekend. "Search and rescue operations have been temporarily halted because it is raining, and the weather is foggy," Narendra Pariyar, a top official for Nepal's Rasuwa district, told Reuters. MORE THAN 3,000 MISSING AFTER COLOMBIA EARTHQUAKE AS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROVIDES $15.5 MILLION IN RELIEF While Nepalese authorities have stressed they don't need countries to send people to help with general search and rescue, they did request that China send tunnel experts as up to 100 people are still trapped in a mud-filled hydropower plant tunnel. ARMY BLACK HAWKS AIRLIFT 200-PLUS STRANDED CAMPERS AS MISSOURI FLOODS TRIGGER MORE 350 RESCUES "We have already made requests for such specialised services and technical assistance in areas where we don't have enough expertise and technical know-how," Nepal's Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told Reuters. China dispatched five such workers from Tibet by helicopter to assist, according to the country's state-affiliated Xinhua news agency. COLOMBIA BUILDING COLLAPSES ON CAMERA AS EARTHQUAKE BRINGS DEATH, DESTRUCTION Dramatic video showed the rescue of one such person as authorities from Nepal worked to drag the man out of the mud deluge. Though impending rainstorms are likely to make rescue operations more difficult, officials say a previous threat from a lake that had formed on the border between Nepal and Tibet has substantially subsided. MASSIVE GARBAGE HEAP COLLAPSES ONTO HOMES, KILLING AT LEAST 30 AS RESCUERS SEARCH FOR SURVIVORS The lake had been overflowing into the Lhende Khola River, risking further flooding, but that risk had gone down by Saturday, according to Chinese officials. articles.title: BFSI firms drive India’s GCC office leasing as demand shifts beyond tech
articles.summary: News News: Foreign banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) companies significantly increased their office space leasing for global capability centres (G.
articles.body: Foreign banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) companies significantly increased their office space leasing for global capability centres (GCCs) in India during the first half of 2026, while demand from foreign IT-ITeS firms declined, Knight Frank India data showed.BFSI companies leased 7.32 million sq ft of office space across eight major cities between January and June, up 70% from 4.31 million sq ft in the same period last year. Their share stood at 36% of the total 20.6 million sq ft leased for GCCs across the eight markets.The cities covered in the data were Mumbai, Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Ahmedabad and Kolkata.The sharp rise in BFSI leasing came alongside a 28% decline in office space taken by foreign IT-ITeS companies for GCCs. Their leasing fell to 4.13 million sq ft in the first six months of 2026 from 5.71 million sq ft a year earlier."India's commercial real estate market is witnessing a clear structural shift, with GCC-led demand becoming increasingly diversified beyond traditional technology occupiers," said Viral Desai, international partner, senior executive director, Occupier Strategy Solutions, Industrial & Logistics, Capital Markets & Retail, Knight Frank India.The 70% year-on-year surge in BFSI-led GCC transactions underscores the sector's growing appetite for high-quality office spaces, he added.Demand from other service companies moved in the opposite direction, with their office leasing rising to 5.10 million sq ft from 4.41 million sq ft during the period.Desai noted that the strong growth in other service sectors points to a broader expansion of India's services economy."The moderation in IT/ITeS absorption reflects a period of recalibration as occupiers realign their global strategies. This evolving demand profile highlights the increasing depth and resilience of India's commercial real estate market, with BFSI emerging as a key driver of office space demand in 2026," Desai said.Global manufacturing companies also reduced their GCC-related office leasing, with absorption declining to 4.05 million sq ft in January-June 2026 from 4.67 million sq ft in the year-ago period.Accuspace managing director Mukesh Choudhary said, "India's GCC ecosystem is entering a decisive phase of expansion, with state-level policies, skilled workforce, incentives and infrastructure commitments creating a strong pipeline of new centres and employment".The scale of GCC additions and diversification is likely to translate into sustained demand for quality office space, not just in established hubs but also across emerging markets, Choudhary added.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Americans don't always want to move to coastal cities for tech jobs, leaving families: Indian-origin founder Apoorva Govind explains why companies have to hire H-1Bs
articles.summary: US News: Amid a renewed controversy over whether American jobs should be reserved for Americans and not skilled foreigners, Indian-origin tech leader Apoorva G.
articles.body: Amid a renewed controversy over whether American jobs should be reserved for Americans and not skilled foreigners, Indian-origin tech leader Apoorva Govind presented a detailed analysis of the tech situation, breaking down which tech companies need what type of skills. Govind said she had been in tech for 15 years now and witnessed that a lot of Americans value living close to their family and friends. "They don't want to move to the coastal cities where all the tech jobs are concentrated. So sometimes the employers are left with no choice but to hire foreign nationals," Govind said, adding that it also means that more states need to create tech hubs like Pittsburgh, Raleigh, and Dallas/Austin have.Govind explained that there are three types of companies that hire techies. In the first type, there are companies like Apple and Google that offer many jobs, but one has to crack the interview and move to the city where they are based. H-1Bs are about 2-3% of the workforce in these companies and most of them have a Master's/ PhD from American universities. "These H1Bs command premium market-rate salaries. These are highly coveted, talented people who any country would be lucky to have," she said.The second category is startups and not many H-1Bs want to work with them because of the uncertainty and Americans do not apply. Govind said that when she was recruiting for Bestever AI, she wanted to hire Americans because the overhead to hire a foreign national was much but there were only a few applications from US-born applicants. "If startups are hiring H1Bs it's because there is no other option (It's 100% not the cheap option). The cheaper option is to hire remote," she said.About 60% of tech jobs fall in the third category which are tech jobs in non-tech companies -- tech jobs in banks, health care etc."This 3rd category of jobs are also the ones that get contracted out to companies like Wipro/Infosys etc who then turn around and import software engineers from abroad (who they then underpay). THIS is the category that's rife with H1B abuse. The employees are not nearly as talented or risk-taking as the other categories. There is no reason why we import people from abroad for these roles. If the Trump admin wants to fix the H1B problem, they need to go to their bank, healthcare and retail CEOs and ask them to crack down, not their Silicon Valley CEOs," Govind argued.Apoorva Govind said the third category should be targeted as the first, two categories require highly technical people, unlike the third."The recent post that spoke derisively about "flyover cities" is despicable and as an immigrant I found it to be disgustingly elitist. It doesn't help address the real problem which is abuse of H1 by certain employers while there is shortage of talent elsewhere," Govind said, referring to the controversy triggered by YC Partner Ankit Gupta.The H-1b visa and Silicon Valley are again at the center of a raging controversy after the administration revised the H-1B fee to around $103K and vice president JD Vance said Americans should be prioritized for American jobs. Silicon Valley leaders did not agree and they said skilled people should be hired notwithstanding their nationality. The issue became bigger with government officials taking note of Y Combinator partner Ankit Gupta defense of H-1B visa holders and his apparent derision towards Americans.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: RSS chief’s visit to US denounced as ‘goodwill tour’ for Hindu nationalism
articles.summary: Activists say Hindu nationalists have sought to mask far-right politics through broad appeals to the Indian diaspora.
articles.body:
An event in New York City featuring a prominent Hindu nationalist is being promoted as an invitation to send a positive message that “the world is one family”.

But an array of faith groups, advocacy organisations and unprivileged-caste organisations say they are not convinced. They fear Saturday’s rally, held at Madison Square Garden, is instead a high-profile effort to whitewash a record of discrimination and violence.

At issue is the Universal Oneness Celebration, hosted by the American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue, a nonprofit that purports to advance “greater peace and harmony”.

One of its keynote speakers, however, will be Mohan Bhagwat, the leader of the Hindu paramilitary organisation Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). His organisation has been accused of embracing discriminatory policies and stoking violence against minorities, including India’s Muslim, Christian and Sikh populations.

Protests are expected outside Madison Square Garden to denounce Bhagwat’s appearance.

“This is a movement that has normalised mob violence against Muslims, attacks on Muslim men in relationships with Hindu women and the bulldozing of Muslim homes,” said Safa Ahmed, a Muslim community organiser in North Carolina who has travelled to New York to join the protests.

She told Al Jazeera she is sceptical about the event organisers’ claims about embracing the world as “one family”.

“They may speak about unity, but it’s in stark contrast with the bloody reality faced by minorities in India,” she said.

Advocates say that Hindu nationalist groups are working to expand their influence in the United States, where roughly 2.5 million Hindus live.

To do that, they have utilised a variety of appeals to soften the image of the RSS, such as celebrations of Hindu culture and campaigns to highlight anti-Hindu discrimination.

Sravya Tadepalli, the deputy executive director of Hindus for Human Rights, sees Saturday’s rally as part of that trend. Her group opposes the event.

“This is kind of a goodwill tour to improve the public image of the RSS, which is a fascist paramilitary organisation that has engaged in decades of communal violence against religious minorities in South Asia,” Tadepalli told Al Jazeera.

“The organisations behind this have pitched it as a broad appeal to Hindu history with an emphasis on inclusivity when, in reality, the RSS advocates for the exact opposite.”

Critics have pointed out, however, that Hindu nationalists have also sought to cultivate links with the global far-right, emphasising a shared belief in the purported threats posed by Islam and secular elites.

The RSS is widely considered the ideological parent of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which has ruled India since 2014 and sought to remake the country along Hindu nationalist lines.

In remarks to the 2024 National Conservatism Conference in Washington, DC, BJP Vice President Ram Madhav said that conservatives in the West should view India as an example of how to defeat what he called the “left, liberal, Marxist, radical Islamist cabal”.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who entered politics as an RSS cadre before becoming the head of the BJP, has championed Hindu nationalism throughout his leadership.

Like Bhagwat, he has also taken his message on the road, to speak to overseas supporters in the US.

In September 2019, for instance, the prime minister addressed a crowd of 50,000 at a “Howdy, Modi!” rally in the state of Texas.

The event underscored Modi’s appeal among Indians living abroad and was one of the largest such events in US history. US President Donald Trump, another far-right leader, even joined Modi on stage.

But such appearances were controversial too. Before becoming prime minister in 2014, Modi was banned from entering the US because of his leadership during a 2002 massacre of Muslim residents in the state of Gujarat.

Modi faced accusations of turning a blind eye to the slayings and even offering his support.

Even as he faces protests, though, Modi remains enormously popular in India, consistently ranking as one of the most popular leaders in the world. A survey this month from the magazine India Today found that he is also the top choice for prime minister in India, despite slipping approval ratings.

Still, outreach campaigns to rehabilitate the image of the RSS overseas have had limited success.

For instance, a 2024 survey found that, while Modi enjoyed near-majority support among Indian Americans for his performance as prime minister, 70 percent of respondents acknowledged that his rhetoric exemplified a growing threat to minorities in India.

Bhagwat’s planned appearance at Madison Square Garden has likewise ignited debate over his controversial commentary and leadership.

In a statement on Wednesday, the US Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF), an independent initiative within the federal government, called for Bhagwat’s visa to be revoked.

The commission warned that Bhagwat was “complicit in religious freedom violations”, along with other RSS members and Indian officials.

“Religious freedom conditions in India continue to deteriorate as violence and incitement are frequently used to target religious minority communities,” said USCIRF Chair Asif Mahmood. He urged the US to implement targeted sanctions.

When questioned about Bhagwat’s speech at a news conference this week, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani also spoke out against the RSS’s messaging.

“It has been incredibly troubling to see the rise of a movement that is predicated on an exclusionary vision of any country, frankly. And it is one that I find myself in deep opposition to,” Mamdani said, citing his identity as an Indian American.

He added that he does not “support the rally” but said he doubted the city had the jurisdiction to cancel a private event.

Ahmed, the community organiser from North Carolina, said she feels the backlash to Saturday’s event reflects a growing coalition in the Indian diaspora — one that brings together Hindu, Muslim, Sikh and unprivileged-caste voices.

“There is a vocal minority in the diaspora and a new, emerging majority who don’t believe in the politics of Modi and the RSS and who don’t want to see them gain traction here,” said Ahmed.

She predicted that Saturday’s event will ultimately backfire. “I’m very confident that Bhagwat will be met with a resounding rejection that he is not welcome.”

articles.title: DAVID MARCUS: Woke Virginia tears down statue of Geneva Convention pioneer
articles.summary: Hunter Holmes McGuire's statue was removed from Richmond capitol grounds despite his role in creating the Winchester Accord.
articles.body: Do not adjust your calendars. You may have seen images this week of Confederate statues coming down in Richmond’s capitol grounds, and thought we had slipped back in time to the tumult of 2020, but no. Rather, the commie Commonwealth of Virginia is still tearing down American history in the year of our Lord 2026. As bad as the removal of all of these monuments has been, this particular round of damnatio memoriae on Friday, captured in its illiberal net the statue of a man named Dr. Hunter Holmes McGuire, whose work provided a major contribution to the Geneva Convention, the global gold standard of wartime humanitarian rules. McGuire served as a Confederate surgeon for almost the entirety of the Civil War, saving countless lives. One life he failed to save was that of General Thomas "Stonewall" Jackson, who died under the doctor’s care. A Jackson statue also came down on Friday. GENDER EQUITY, DEI, CLIMATE ACTION: HOW THE SMITHSONIAN'S WOKE PUSH 'INFILTRATED' AMERICA'S MOST BELOVED ZOO Once again, the good Dr. McGuire could not save Stonewall. It was under Jackson’s command in 1862 that McGuire established a new humanitarian principle of warfare that we still have with us today, not just in the United States, but across the world. In May 1862, after the First Battle of Winchester, 6 Union army doctors were captured. It was then that McGuire convinced a reluctant Jackson to release them, and established, with Northern agreement, the Winchester Accord, after which both sides released doctors as non-combatants. McGuire himself would be released by the North under the accord in 1864, and would go on to be present for the Confederate surrender at Appomattox Courthouse. The Winchester Accord would be adopted by the Geneva Convention, offering protection to medical personnel in wars that they still enjoy today, and yet, despite all of this, his statue was toppled, just like all the others. As usual, the destroyers of monuments brook no nuance in their march to destroy American history. If you wore the wrong uniform, your statue has to go and you have to be disgraced. According to Democratic state Senator Mike Jones, McGuire’s statue had to be removed because, "I remembered seeing white only, colored only pictures in my mother’s scrapbook, and so to have that as a visual and then for these things to remain to remind this area of what took place, I think it’s wrong." I’m sorry, but the fact that Jones is made uneasy by metal statues because they remind him of racism that occurred 70 years ago is the kind of silly claptrap that should have been left in the madness of 2020, and yet here we are. Allow me to go a bit further and argue that if you took the accomplishments of every person involved with having McGuire’s statue removed, they would not begin to equal his contributions to the humanization of modern military conflict. It really is incredible. Day and night, night and day, the progressive left goes on and on about alleged war crimes committed by Israel, or the United States, and yet in their ignorance and simple-mindedness they are defaming a man who played a key role in creating the definitions of those very alleged crimes. TRUMP V.
